author: Nichola B
title: AVOID if you’re travelling to New York as a family!
text:
Long review but a very honest review! I don’t normally review but this one I had to.

We stayed at this hotel for 5 nights at the beginning of August 2026 as part of my our 40th birthday trip. New York was our final stop after San Francisco, Las Vegas and Orlando, where we’d had fantastic experiences and amazing service. Unfortunately, this hotel was a completely different story and ended what had otherwise been an incredible trip on a very sour note.

Things went wrong almost immediately.

The hotel arranged for a a taxi transfer company to contact us to arrange pick up from the airport, which we thought would make things much easier after a long journey. The driver asked for our name and hotel, so we assumed everything was correct. We arrived at what we thought was our hotel, only for reception to tell us we were at the “other Hampton Inn.” We then had to collect all our luggage and walk to the correct hotel.
How would we have known there were other Hampton Inn hotels?! Surely the taxi transfer company knows this so why didn’t they ask us to be specific?! And why didn’t they know which one we were going to when the hotel arranged the contact? 

We were exhausted by the time we arrived, so despite everything, we decided not to complain and just wanted to get some food and go to bed.

Then we discovered one of the lifts was out of order. We were on the 16th floor, and it took around 15–20 minutes to get the remaining lift.

When we finally got to our room, we were genuinely shocked by how small it was. We were a family of four — two adults, a 14-year-old and a 9-year-old — and there was virtually no space at all. We couldn’t unpack because there simply wasn’t anywhere to put our belongings, so we had to live out of our suitcases for the entire stay.

The shower was also ridiculously small. My husband is 6ft 1 and actually banged his head several times while showering.

That first evening, we returned from dinner hoping to relax and watch some TV for an hour. The TV didn’t work.

We tried calling reception — the phone in our room didn’t work either.

That is particularly concerning when you are on the 16th floor and already have one lift out of service. In an emergency, being unable to contact reception from your room is a serious issue.

My husband went down to reception and reported the problems. We were told someone would come up.

By 10.30pm, we were exhausted and had to go to sleep.

The following day, we went out expecting that the issues would be sorted while we were away.

They weren’t.

When we returned, our room hadn’t been serviced at all. The towels we had used that morning were still on the floor, the beds hadn’t been made, and the TV was still not working.

I went down to reception and spoke to Andy, who apologised for everything — the wrong hotel transfer, the lift, the TV, the phone and the lack of room service.

He looked into moving us to a bigger room, but said there were no larger rooms available. He then offered Hilton points as compensation. As we aren’t Hilton members, this wasn’t particularly useful to us.

I asked whether there was any possibility of a refund so we could leave and stay somewhere else for the remaining four nights. Andy told me that this could be arranged, but that we needed to contact the company we had booked through. He explained that they would contact the hotel and the hotel would then confirm that we could leave and receive a refund.

At this point, we genuinely thought we were getting somewhere.

Unfortunately, the following morning my husband spoke to the General Manager, who told him that the information we had been given was incorrect and that we could not leave and receive a refund.

We were also told there were no larger rooms because the hotel doesn’t actually have larger rooms. So when Andy had looked into moving us to a bigger room, there was never actually a bigger room to move us to.

We were essentially stuck.

What disappointed us most was what happened afterwards. Following our conversation with the General Manager, not one member of staff checked in with us for the rest of our stay.

Not to ask if everything was okay.

Not to apologise.

Not to ask whether we wanted the Hilton points that had previously been offered.

Nothing.

On our final night, we returned to find that our room hadn’t been cleaned again, meaning we didn’t even have fresh towels for the following morning when we were flying home.

By that point, I honestly had no energy left to complain again.

Having now read back through some of the other reviews, I can see that comments about staff not seeming to care and problems being brushed aside are sadly very similar to our own experience.

This hotel completely let us down.

We will never stay here again, and although we absolutely love New York and will return, we will definitely be choosing a different hotel next time.

It’s such a shame because this was supposed to be a special 40th birthday trip. San Francisco, Las Vegas and Orlando had all been fantastic, with brilliant service throughout. Unfortunately, our experience here left us feeling incredibly disappointed and frustrated at the end of what had otherwise been an amazing holiday.

If you’re travelling to New York with a family, I would seriously recommend looking elsewhere.

author: John S

author: Getaway11612799129
title: If you or someone you love has a disability or travel with a mobility device, read this before booking at this hotel.
text:
I stayed here in August 2026 while attending conferences nearby. My disability relapses unpredictably, and when symptoms returned a few weeks before the trip I tried to modify or cancel my reservation and could not, because I had booked through Expedia (which apparently forfeited all rights as a human). The hotel's website showed accessible rooms available that week, so I requested a low floor in the Hilton app and had my power chair delivered to the hotel ahead of my arrival.

Zay M. the front desk manager, checked me in arranged for my chair to be brought out to me at the front desk. Even so, I was never offered an accessible room. I had requested the 3rd floor and was assigned the 29th. No one said a word about any rules for the chair, including any rule against bringing it into my room, which is how I get around (and the manager even pointed to where the elevators where so I could access my room while I was in the chair).

The room's entryway was tight and there was a mirror in the entryway, and that evening the chair cracked the mirror. I reported it to the front desk myself within minutes and said I probably needed an ADA accommodation. The employee, Marwane, who answered responded with real care: they asked if I was okay, apologized that no accessible rooms were open that night, offered to remove the mirror and shift furniture so I could move safely, and promised to keep checking ADA availability. I said I could make do for the night. If it had ended there, this would be a different review.

Instead Zay M. took over the conversation and the tone turned accusatory. I was told I had never mentioned my mobility issues to him when I checked in. This is the same manager who had my power chair brought to me at check-in. I was told I should not have brought the chair into the room, and that I would pay for the mirror, later quoted to me at $400. It should be noted the hallway outside of the rooms are not wide enough to walk around if my chair was parked there.

I asked to speak with someone else and was told there was no one else and that he was the only manager. When I called Hilton's guest assistance line that evening, the representative checked with the hotel and came back saying I had been offered an ADA accommodation and declined it (probably in reference to my purchase on Expedia in March). That is not what happened, and it contradicts what the hotel's own staff had texted me an hour earlier.

I left that night, in a thunderstorm, and another hotel had an accessible room ready for me within an hour. Between the forfeited nights, the mirror charge, and a last-minute room elsewhere, this stay cost me well over a thousand dollars. It was my first trip without my caregiver for an academic conference that I am presenting at. I would much better have been preparing for that, than writing this review.

There was no understanding of ADA, no understanding of customer service, and there seemed to be way more interest in punishing and dehumanizing guests with disabilities than welcoming them.

author: Alejandra R

author: Fabio B

At this hotel, I paid for the breakfast-included package and upon our arrival, you discover that the package includes ONLY ONE item per person.
So, after waiting in line for 20 minutes, you can take only 1 yogurt, only 1 egg, and so on.

author: Stefano A
title: Very slow breakfast and at checkout they do whatever they want
text:
We stayed at this hotel from August 4th to the 13th.
Positive notes:
 location, comfortable beds and comfortable bathroom, room cleaning more or less at the usual time and quite fast, satisfactory air conditioning, closet a bit small but several drawers. 
Negative notes:
Breakfast 
the products are good but the service is very slow and there is little attention to refilling products (since the breakfast formula involves choosing three products from 3 categories: 1 preparation, 1 fruit, 1 drink.... it often happened that the fruit ran out and was not replaced with another option).... poor maintenance of the coffee machine.... sometimes I was left waiting for someone to come and put water in... without being able to make coffee!
Resort fee....29 dollars that become 33.35 with taxes...which they grant you as credit to spend at the hotel bar..convenient but with little control.... so much so that at the time of checkout when we had to redeem the 400 dollar deposit (50 for 8 nights) requested at check-in, we were told that the resort fees for the 9 nights would be deducted from that amount...so a total...a week after returning we see from the credit card that they withheld another 96 dollars but it is not known for what reason because at checkout they did not communicate anything.... we have already sent two emails to get explanations and details of the expenses but we have not received a response... we are waiting!

author: Maria M
title: Room
text: Jonathan and Zaida have been absolutely amazing!! They’re both so nice, attentive, and have made my stay such a great experience. I still have an hour left, but I already know I’ll definitely be coming back to this hotel because of them! ❤️

author: Lori B
title: 2nd Stay - Great Experience
text:
This was my second multi-night stay at this hotel. It’s conveniently located within easy walking distance of Javits Center and close to Times Square and restaurants. I like the size of this hotel - about 120 rooms. The room was clean, modern/ updated and my premium king room had a fancy Nespresso coffee maker. I was not an immediate fan of the resort fee but soon learned how to make the daily food credit in the hotel lounge work for me as the prices there are much more reasonable than food prices at Javits. 
The staff at this hotel is what brought me back for this return stay of 4 nights. They are really friendly and go out of their way to ask about your stay, room, check-in, and genuinely want to know if they can do anything for you. In my experience this is truly unique in hotels almost anywhere these days but particularly in New York City. I was literally greeted by name when I came through the lobby on several occasions!
Special shout out to front desk staff members Robbi and Jonathan for the extra attention and assistance and great efficiency . Also thanks to Neisha (overnight front desk) who took great care of me upon my very early morning arrival at the hotel until my room was ready. She was very gracious, supplied beverages and checked in frequently about my comfort and wellbeing. 
These are just the people I interacted with the most. All the staff members were friendly and efficient. This hotel delivers really well on all the basics but the staff sets the hotel apart and take the experience to another level!

author: PrincessCaro
title: The distrikt rocks
text: Beautiful quiet and super comfy beds. My new favorite hotel for my work visits to Manhattan. Jon did an amazing job!

author: Alfredo S
title: Good hotel to recommend.
text:
Excellent hotel in the border of a bad area of Rome.
They have a front desk open 24 hours and extra staff to take you in and out.
They gave a special deal for 118 Euros per room, which we appreciated.
Nearby are good restaurants and coffee shops.
It is located a couple of blocks from the Termini Station.

author: Summerfamilytrip22
title: A 206€ hold for a month, ants in the room, and a lack of transparency!
text: Terrible experience on July 4th for a two-hour afternoon stay. Although the request was for 106€, I paid 100€ in cash (they even wanted the reservation..). They made problems with my foreign boyfriend's document.. another 15 minutes lost. The hotel still blocked another 206€ from my card left as a guarantee. On the phone and via email (contacted 5 times) they teased me for weeks saying they had made the manual reversal, but the money only returned on August 7th, creating a serious financial inconvenience for me. The room also had hundreds of ants on the floor; when we left and I pointed it out to the reception, they dismissed me with a simple "ah thanks for the report," without apologizing. Furthermore, on the table they leave snacks that seem like a welcome gift, only to then hide a tiny note that declares everything except water is for a fee. A truly unfair way to make money on every detail. Beautiful and aesthetically elegant structure, but unreliable management. Highly unrecommended.

author: Sieuwke V
title: Most hospitable hotel in the universe!
text:
This hotel is absolutely highly recommended!
I had contacted them to ask if it was possible to work remotely at their facility. Already from the email exchange, I had perceived a truly warm and kind welcome, so much so that I couldn't wait to come! They responded very quickly and with truly special cordiality.

Now I am here and I am immensely grateful to have had the opportunity to come: this place is simply wonderful! And it is not just the beauty of the facility: as soon as I arrived, I was welcomed with truly extraordinary kindness and efficiency.

I needed an adapter for the electrical outlet and they immediately found a solution. Furthermore, I was served the best cappuccino I have ever drunk, accompanied by two cookies "to keep me company". Such a thoughtful gesture really struck me!

It is a shame to be here only to work today: I would love to spend an entire vacation as a guest of this hotel. Without a doubt, I will return in the future to turn this wish into reality. It was truly a fantastic experience.

Thanks to the most hospitable hotel in the universe! ;-)

author: Arnold P

author: Diane V
title: First trip to NY!
text:
I never write reviews but felt compelled because this hotel and location really made my trip with my husband to NY a truly lovely and wonderful experience. We were first timers in NY and didn't know quite what to expect.  This location was central to everything with tons of nice restaurants and bars at your fingertips. We strolled Bryant Park multiple times as it was simply beautiful and they had so many activities throughout the week including bands, morning yoga, cocktails, and so many food choices to enjoy in the beautiful park surroundings. You can walk, taxi or subway to all major locations so we did not feel overwhelmed in the least. Would love to come back here at Christmas time to partake in the festivities!
Special shout out to Arlette snd Yovanni for their wonderful hospitality!

author: Shouq A

Yovanni and Arlette made the process extremely easy and were accommodating to all our needs. Will definitely come back

author: Melissa m
title: amazing stay
text: room was very small, but then again the square footage was posted when i booked. but for 1 night for a single person or a couple it was more than what we needed. room was clean and modern. bar was great, great view, great drinks. great, central location. staff was incredibly welcoming and helpful. i even left some items and the hotel went out of their way in getting my things returned to me. will def stay again.

author: ADVISOR T
title: Great Stay at the Artezen
text:
I had a fantastic stay and would definitely recommend this hotel.

The location is excellent and incredibly convenient for enjoying New York. The entire staff was great, genuinely kind, respectful, welcoming, and always very helpful whenever I needed anything.

The room was comfortable, and having a private terrace was a real bonus, especially considering the price. It added a lot to the experience and made the stay feel even more special. I also have to mention how comfortable the bed and pillows were. I honestly had some of the best sleep I’ve had in a long time!

The only area that could use some improvement is the furniture in the rooms. Some of the wardrobes, tables, and other pieces feel a little dated and would benefit from being renewed or modernized.

Apart from that, everything was excellent. Great location, wonderful staff, comfortable rooms, and very good value for New York. I had a great stay and would happily come back!

author: Darren L
title: Excellent hotel
text:
We had a 5 night stay at this excellent hotel. We had booked it directly with the hotel. The location is great. We like the downtown area and very convenient for subway stations.
The room was 1402 and it was very stylish and looked to be fairly recently refurbished. Bed was very comfortable. There was a fridge and a nespresso machine. Very nice bathroom with great shower. Only negative was the wardrobe was very small.
The housekeepers do a great job. Everything was very clean. Reception staff all pleasant and helpful. 
There is a very nice rooftop bar which we went to one evening and they have a good happy hour.
All in all a great stay. We would definitely come back here and recommend.

author: janw597
title: The Artezen ~ A Great Place to Stay for a New York Getaway!
text:
My family and I stayed at the Artezen Hotel in New York for four nights. I could not have been more impressed with the service, the staff, the daily delivery of water to our room and the truly exceptional feeling of being welcomed and greeted every time we entered the building. 

The rooms were clean and very comfortable. The price was extremely reasonable. The location to the subway was convenient and there were many restaurants, shops and sites to see that were within walking distance.

It was August and the weather was very hot, yet after a day of sightseeing ~ it really was wonderful to come back to the comfort of the Artezen Hotel.

author: Suzy R
title: Such a wonderful calm base for exploring NYC
text: My partner and I recently stayed at The Artezen for 4 nights when visiting NYC.  It was such a lovely experience that I wanted to share.  The hotel team are really lovely and friendly and helpful and polite.  They always gave us a warm welcome whether it was coming down from the room or going out or coming back in.  Always opening the doors for us.  Concierge is lovely, especially Juan.  It was a fab location just a short walk to Wall Street but actually we walked to China Town and Little Italy it wasn't far away.  There are lots of shops, take aways on the doorstep along with the subway.  I was worried it may be too far from the buzz of Times Square etc but it was a perfect little oasis to come back to at the end of a busy hot New York day.  It was really quiet and the AC worked a treat and was very quiet too.  Room was fab and so clean.  Bed was amazing and we had the best sleeps.  Thank you Artezen - we would like to come back.

author: Mark P
title: Great location for tube
text:
Location very good as tube station just a few minutes walk and a nice pub over the road and a nice restaurant connected to hotel.
The staff were lovely and friendly through out and helpful.
When we went to the rooms there was a strong smell of musty damp and this continued when we went in our room. 
The room itself was clean and tidy so no complaints there. we bought an air fresher and that did the trick for the musty smell.
The wi-fi was very bad but as only in room to sleep wasn't to mush of a problem if i had spent more time in hotel would of wanted the internet more.

author: Emmaharris2015
title: Good location and good food next door
text:
We chose this hotel as it was recommended on the Amex app with a deal.
The hotel is well situated and easy to get to with plenty of transport near by and amenities. 
The hotel is connected to a Chaiiwala restaurant which was lovely, and the breakfast included in the hotel payment was there, it was great each morning, coming with chicken sausages, turkey bacon, hashbrowns, beans, egg and toast. However, if you wanted English breakfast tea – it wasn’t an option and the teabags given were chai.
We love Indian food and they had a great choice for lunch.
You can also pay £5 each day to access the gym 2 doors down.
There are several pubs within walking distance, lots of takeaways and shops locally too.
The rooms are clean but very basic and in need of some modernisation. 

As we were visiting in summer, I was relieved to discover air conditioning which worked well! I would have appreciated some water in the room, when I asked the front desk whether I could get water he told me to go to Tesco or the local store. Even though I could see a fridge of bottles of water in the lobby. 
The bathroom was not the best, the door to the shower did not have adequate fittings and stayed open whilst showering, flooding the bathroom floor which we had to use our towels each day to soak up. The curtain track in the main room fell down every time we opened or closed the curtains. 
When we went out for the day, despite putting the housekeeping request on the door and switching on the designated light to indicate the room was ready to be cleaned, we would return to hotel around 3pm-4pm to get ready for our evenings and the rooms had not been turned down, had twice ran out of toilet roll and had no clean/dry towels to use, this happened every day. The rooms would be done by the time we returned at 10pm or so, but I really think that guests staying should be a priority. 

Immediate recommendations to elevate the hotel would be:
-	More milk sachets provided in room for teas and coffees.
-	Water in the rooms.
-	Wine glasses in the rooms for guests to use. 
-	Fix shower fittings. 
-	Fix curtain poles.
-	Get housekeeping to do service earlier in the day. 

Nevertheless, based on the location, the cost and the breakfast at Chaiiwala, I would consider staying again, its not the worst place to settle after long days out.

author: Kim C
title: Damp and smelly
text:
The location is handy for underground stations. We had a basement room and the room was just damp . The bedding and soft furnishings were all damp and it smelled really bad. We barely slept as we basically slept in a bed that was damp. 
there was a leak above the shower which was dripping constantly.

author: Emma L
title: Excellent hotel for the price
text:
This is our 5th time staying at the hotel and will definitely be returning. 
Our room was spacious and clean, with tea and coffee facilities. 
The bed was comfortable, providing us with a good nights sleep and the climate control was perfect, considering we visited during the recent heatwave.
Staff are friendly and helpful, greeting us with a cold lemonade on arrival.
Location is fantastic, 3 stops from Paddington which is great for exploring London.
We highly recommend as it’s such good value for money!

author: Sally W
title: Fabulous weekend in London
text: So my partner booked this hotel for our weekend in London to see Lewis Capaldi. London was very busy the weekend of 10th-12th July and we did pay over the odds. We had never stayed this side of London before and after reading the reviews it is safe to say I was very anxious and worried. When we arrived at Kilburn High road I was a bit concerned initially as I walked out, but once we had checked in and walked around we both really liked it. The receptionist was lovely and very friendly. We had a nice room, clean, working tv, working air con, clean bathroom no concerns AT ALL!  We always explore our area on arrival and it is clear other people don’t do the same. We found some cracking pubs on our doorstep, The Old Bell with a lovely outdoor area across the road and some other fab pubs in walking distance. We also found the wonderful  Paddington recreation ground just 10 minutes away. We have never had anything like this in London. A little cafe, kids play area, football courts, tennis courts, athletics track, large field where there was a cricket match taking place, forests and areas of nature, beautiful little gardens. We loved it that much we went for a walk the following morning before heading out for the day. The overground was 7 mins to Euston and everywhere else very easy to get around. Everyone we came across was polite end friendly and we loved it so much we would definitely return! We even went to one of the local pubs after the concert for the second half of the England quarter final football game along with extra time. The bar staff were so friendly and we had no issues at all. Absolutely fabulous weekend in London and would recommend, just keep an open mind. You are in a massive capital city at the end of the day! I appreciate everyone’s experiences are different but we can only comment on ours.

author: KateyKate
title: Great hotel, nice staff
text: Great location, nice room, lovely helpful staff

author: Travel03158040976
title: NCY adventure
text: I wanted to take a moment to express how absolutely incredible our stay was. Everything exceeded our expectations! The room was beautiful, far better than we could have ever imagined. The staff was incredibly welcoming and professional, making us feel at home from the very first moment. The breakfast was phenomenal and the value for money was truly unbelievable for such a prime location. Thank you for an unforgettable NYC adventure, we will definitely be recommending your hotel to everyone we know!!

author: JJH04
title: Good location, small rooms, but very clean
text:
Just had a nice two nights stay for a daughter mother trip to go see The Lost Boys. Location is very close to Amtrak and the bus station so good on that mark. About a 10 minute walk and you are in Times Square.
The rooms were clean, but small very small but again very clean. With two queen beds there wasn’t much room to move around, but we’re both adults and we weren’t spending all of our time in the room. Just wanted to forewarn anybody that’s traveling with small kids that needs more space. This may not be the place for you.
Hotel staff was very nice. Didn’t really have the breakfast, but the coffee wasn’t bad.

author: Francisco C
title: “Very disappointing experience — poor service and promises not kept”
text:
I had a very disappointing experience at SpringHill Suites by Marriott in Manhattan.

When I arrived, the room I had originally reserved was not available, so I was given a different room instead. Unfortunately, I had to stay in that room for the entire duration of my stay.

To make matters worse, during the first three nights, my room was not cleaned at all. The beds were not made and the towels were not changed. I complained to the front desk, and after raising the issue again, I was told that this should not have happened and that I would receive a $100 discount on my room as compensation.

However, when it was time to pay, I was told that there was no record of the $100 discount and that nothing could be done. This was extremely frustrating. If a member of the staff makes a commitment to a guest, it should be properly documented and honored. Otherwise, it becomes very difficult to trust what guests are being told.

I also found my interactions with Natasha, Jeffrey, Eric, and William to be particularly disappointing and unprofessional. Whenever I approached them to follow up on my complaints, I felt that I was simply being told “yes, yes, yes” to get me out of the way, without any genuine intention of resolving the problems.

Overall, the combination of being given a different room than the one I had booked, having no housekeeping service for the first three nights, and then being promised compensation that was not honored made this a very poor experience.

I expected much better from a Marriott property. Based on my experience, I would not recommend this hotel.

author: Robert H
title: I would return here
text:
This is standing Hotel for its price range and location! I would very much look forward to staying here again on my next visit to New York City. First, you can’t beat the location. If you desire, you can walk to Penn Station. Light many New York hotels, this was an old building that has been renovated. Whoever your interior designers are did an outstanding job of utilizing the space efficiently, designing the window treatments and artwork, and providing furnishings that are functional and comfortable. 

The dining area downstairs was done extremely well. The staff did a great job of making sure that the food was constantly replenished and this was  a very busy morning. Also, I forgot to mention that every place we went was spotless (with the exception of the small outdoor area  an occasional pigeon might visit).

author: Dale R

author: AF Travel
title: DISGUSTING HOTEL- DO NOT STAY

I stayed in this hotel for one night and it was the  worst hotel I have ever stayed in. Unfortunately we had no other option otherwise we would have not endured this repulsive stay.

We were greeted at reception and it was extremely slow and nothing seemed to be working , it  took over half an hour to check in , the man on reception was extremely unfriendly and unwelcoming. The lobby was the cleanest part of the hotel and even then it wasn’t great!

When we did eventually speak to them about the issues we were met with attitude and dismissal , they moved us to the “best room” and it was just as foul. Felt like it was smart once but has been left .
Reception area was tired  with wall paper coming away from wall .

author: AM
title: Excellent choice in the Financial District
text:
The hotel is not luxury, but for a week in New York it is more than fine. I liked the location a lot: during my first trip I had stayed in Times Square, but I must say that I definitely prefer the financial district. It is quieter, less noisy and allows you to easily reach the Stock Exchange, the World Trade Center, the harbor and other attractions.
The room was clean, also equipped with a small kitchenette. The beds were very comfortable, while the bathroom, although being a bit dated, was still in good condition. The view looked out onto another building, so nothing special.
The breakfast satisfied me: there was a good selection of both sweet and savory.
The only real negative note concerns the elevators, only two and rather dated. One evening I got stuck on the 30th floor: I recommend always carrying your cell phone with you and saving the reception number, because the alarm button doesn't inspire much confidence.

author: AmyM487

author: Aikaterini M

author: Ernest G
text:
We had a really enjoyable stay at Hotel Joyce – Astotel during our trip to Paris. From the moment we arrived, the staff were friendly, welcoming and helpful, which made a great first impression.

The hotel itself was very clean and well maintained, and our room was comfortable and had everything we needed for our stay. After spending long days exploring Paris, it was a nice place to come back to and relax.

One of the things we particularly liked was the complimentary drinks and snacks available at the hotel. It was such a simple touch, but really appreciated after being out sightseeing for several hours. Breakfast was also good and gave us plenty of choice before heading out for the day.

The location worked really well for us too. There are restaurants and shops nearby, and it was easy enough to get around Paris using the Metro or by taxi.

Overall, Hotel Joyce was a great choice for our father-and-son trip. It felt welcoming, comfortable and well looked after throughout our stay. I would happily stay here again on another visit to Paris and would definitely recommend it to others.

5/5 – a lovely hotel and a very enjoyable stay.

author: nitinsjohn
title: **Very Disappointing for a Times Square Hotel**
text:
Very Disappointing for a Times Square Hotel

Unfortunately, our stay at IHG Times Square felt more like a 3-star motel experience than what I expected from a major hotel brand in New York City.

From the moment we arrived, there was very little hospitality—no real welcome, no smiles, and no effort to make guests feel appreciated. I’ve used my Amex to stay at many hotels, and this was easily one of the more disappointing experiences.

The double-bed room was extremely tight with very little space to store luggage or belongings. There was also no refrigerator or microwave in the room, which was surprising.

Housekeeping was another disappointment. They basically made the beds and cleaned the bathroom, but did not restock the coffee area or other supplies, and even left our used coffee mugs sitting there.

The breakfast buffet was probably the biggest rip-off. It was around $42 per person plus a mandatory tip, yet much of the food felt like basic continental breakfast or reheated/microwave-quality food. Definitely not worth the price.

Service when leaving was also lacking. There was no assistance getting our suitcases down to the lobby or loading them into the car, which you would normally expect from a hotel at this price point and location.

To top it off, the room minibar sensor incorrectly charged us for a bottle of champagne that we never used. Thankfully, the receptionist was helpful and removed the charge without an issue.

The location is convenient, but overall the service, room amenities, housekeeping, and value were well below expectations. For the amount you pay to stay in Times Square, I expected significantly better.

author: Richard Richards

author: Alwaysflyingaway

A special thanks to Jacquelin for her wonderful assistance and exceptional hospitality throughout our stay. We will definitely be back!

author: corbes63
title: Excellent stay!
text:
We nearly didn't book this hotel because the reviews seemed a bit hit-and-miss, but we're very glad we did. We’ve previously stayed in a bunch of different places around town.
Pros:
No “destination/resort” fee!
The location felt really safe throughout our stay, and there is visible security around reception during the overnight hours. The hotel is in a nice neighbourhood, just a few minutes' walk from the subway, making it easy to get around the city and away from the crazy of Times Square.
Breakfast was genuinely excellent and far exceeded our expectations. The hotel arranged gluten-free bagels for us on request at check-in, which was greatly appreciated after our emails prior to the stay went unanswered. There was a wide variety of rotating hot and cold options each morning, and honestly, the breakfast was better than what I've experienced in many executive lounges at full-service US hotel brands. The breakfast team worked incredibly hard keeping everything stocked and refreshed, even during the busiest periods.
Housekeeping was fantastic. They always respected the Do Not Disturb sign and never interrupted us unnecessarily. Gloria deserves special recognition for doing an amazing job freshening up our room when we needed service.
Bryant on the afternoon/evening reception shift was also lovely, and incredibly helpful throughout our stay. A special thank you as well to the manager, Dawn, who was outstanding from start to finish and made a real difference to our experience.
One concern we had before arriving was reports of construction noise, but we didn't see or hear any construction during our stay. We actually stayed in two different rooms and both were exceptionally quiet, with no outside noise at all. Some rooms also feature a double-door arrangement that helps reduce noise from the hallway and other guests. With only around 10 rooms per floor, the hotel felt quiet.
Air conditioning was excellent, we had a heat wave whilst there and the rooms were lovely and cool.
And for anyone wondering from a previous review —we checked carefully and found absolutely no signs of bed bugs.
The guest laundry facilities were also very useful, with a single washing machine and dryer available for guests.
As for the negatives, room sizes do vary slightly by shape but are compact as advertised and reported.
Some reception staff were grumpy and unhelpful, which was inconsistent compared to the excellent service we received from others.
Also, one elevator appears to be permanently out of service, leaving only a single lift operating. If you're staying on a higher floor, it's worth allowing extra time, especially during busy periods.
Breakfast can also get quite busy, and you may occasionally need to wait a minute for a table, although the breakfast staff do an outstanding job keeping everything refreshed and flowing smoothly.
Overall this was a great stay for us. The excellent breakfast, quiet rooms, convenient location, strong housekeeping team, and standout staff members made this a very enjoyable stay, and we would happily stay here again. Many thanks to Dawn and the team!

author: Rabbul M
title: Do not recommend
text:
As a Marriott Lifetime member, this is probably one of the worst hotels, not just within the Marriott brand but among all the hotels I’ve stayed at.

I booked a high-floor room, but at check-in I was told none were available. The room had no complimentary water, and when I asked about it, I was told that water is provided “at the hotel’s discretion.” I was eventually given two tiny bottles.

To make matters worse, the room didn’t have air conditioning. Charging nearly $400 per night for a room without AC is simply unacceptable. The lack of basic amenities, combined with poor service and untrained staff, made this an extremely disappointing stay.

author: Experience819960
title: The elevator is a major issue
text: I am currently staying here. The elevator issue is a major problem. I wasn't notified upon check in that my room would be directly  across from the elevator and that I would hear a  clicking noise all night long. I tried to switch rooms the next day but I had online meetings and didnt have a minute to switch at that time. I tried to switch in the evening but all rooms were sold out. I had conversations with the guy who had to sit in the elevator pushing buttons all day and night and he mentioned they were servicing the elevator we were using next week. This is a major issue:(

author: Traveller From London
title: Worst Marriott experience I've ever had in my life - after being Titanium Elite for 10 years
text:
One of the worst hotels I have ever stayed at in my life. I am Marriott Titanium Elite. They were extremely difficult about providing an early check in - even at 1:30PM. The lady who checked me in even lied and said they were sold out so couldnt switch me to a king bed room, despite there being plenty of rooms on sale online. How can they not clean even 1 room between the check out time of 11AM and 1:30PM? I don't expect this inability to provide a room given my loyalty status. 

Only 1 elevator works and takes forever!! The working elevator causes so much noise I can hear it go up and down loudly from inside of my room - its woken me up so many times that my whoop sleep score is the lowest I've ever seen it. 

There is EXTREMELY LOUD DRILLING construction on the road in front of the hotel - i guess this is not their fault, but they should warn guests. The walls are thin and you can hear every single thing outside the room - even if people are chatting you can hear ever word. 

Room is tiny and generally quite awful, even for NYC standards. I presumed it would be bigger given this is a suite hotel, but I didnt check the measurements beforehand. Its basically the same as a Moxy. If you are overweight, you definitely will not fit in the bathroom.

author: Guy R
title: Dreadful experience - massive decline in quality, maintenance, and service
text:
I first stayed at this hotel in 2013, and it was nothing short of wonderful. Thirteen years later, it was my default choice when booking a New York trip for my family's first ever visit to the city. What a massive mistake. Something has gone seriously wrong with this once-amazing property.

The issues began before we even arrived. I emailed several inquiries and reservation amendments, none of which received a reply until I sent multiple follow-ups. Then, the day before arrival, I received an email stating my first-night charge was declined and our entire 6 night booking would be canceled by noon the next day if not settled. I immediately authorized the charge with Amex, replied to the hotel asking them to re-run it, and asked for confirmation. True to form, the hotel ignored my email and my follow-up. I had to call the morning of our arrival to fix it, adding completely unnecessary stress to our trip.

We checked in and went to our "NoMo Balcony Suite" on the penthouse floor, which cost over $1,000 per night. The nightmare truly began when we opened the door. We were hit by an overpowering, awful smell of cat urine and mold. I immediately called reception and was told, "There is nothing we can do tonight, we have no other rooms, we will deal with it tomorrow."

Hoping to get some fresh air, I went to open the balcony door. To my disbelief, the door was bolted shut to the frame. I called reception back, and they told me, "Yes, we’ve had maintenance issues, so we had to block the exit to the balcony." They openly admitted other guests had complained about this. I paid premium rates for a room explicitly marketed and pictured as a balcony suite, only to find the balcony completely inaccessible.

It was 11 PM, and with no alternative rooms offered, we decided to just sleep and find a new hotel the next day. But it got worse. As my two teenage boys got into the sofa bed, they noticed the sheets and adjacent table were covered in a strange grain/powder. I patted the sheets and confirmed they were filthy.

At this point, I had enough. I went down to the lobby and demanded a manager come up to see and smell the room. Fortunately, the shift had changed, and the night manager, Lucas Aponte, was now on duty. Unlike his dismissive predecessor, Lucas was empathetic, helpful, and genuinely caring.

Lucas worked magic. He found us a new room (a downgrade to the 3rd floor, but we weren't being picky at that point), lowered our nightly rate to reflect the downgrade, and gave us drink coupons. Because of the clean replacement room, and entirely thanks to Lucas's excellent service, we decided to stay for the remainder of our trip.

Bottom line: This hotel suffers from poor management, terrible maintenance, and borderline false advertising regarding its rooms. If it weren't for Lucas saving the night, we would have walked out. We will not be returning.

author: Maria O
title: Pretty Hotel
text: Great location.  Room was fairly spare, but had a nice view.  No coffee in the room, but complimentary coffee in the lobby.  Had no cream or milk, though, so had to go to the cafe bar downstairs to get it.  Front desk staff not particularly friendly.  I wish they'd open a rooftop terrace for the views.  Restaurant was pretty.  Cost less than many hotels in the area.

author: Reda G
title: Extremely disappointing stay.
text:
This hotel was a huge letdown from start to finish. The service is simply terrible, especially at check-in, where the staff were unhelpful and unfriendly. Unfortunately, the same attitude could be found throughout the entire property, including every restaurant we visited. No matter what we asked for, the answer always seemed to be “no.” It almost felt as if the staff were determined to make our stay as unpleasant as possible.

After arriving exhausted from a long international flight, there was absolutely no effort made to welcome us. No flexibility, no consideration, and no sense of hospitality.

The rooms are very average and clearly in need of refurbishment. The aluminum fixtures look old, the headboards are damaged, and some of the curtains are torn. The air conditioning barely works, making the room uncomfortable. There is no coffee machine and not even complimentary water in the room, which is surprising for a hotel of this standard.

The restaurants are also disappointing: neither comfortable nor welcoming, with service that matches the poor experience elsewhere in the hotel.

What disappointed us the most was the lack of hospitality. A beautiful property can never compensate for staff who make guests feel unwelcome. We left feeling frustrated and disappointed, and we would not recommend this hotel.

author: Stephgaorom
title: Terrible
text: Terrible experience with this hotel. The staff is not friendly at all. I was charged without my authorization, and after more than 4 months, the refund is still “being processed.” Very disappointing. Avoid staying here also We paid for a specific room, but when we arrived, they gave us a completely different one because the hotel was fully booked. Their response was: “Tomorrow we’ll see what we can do, there’s nothing we can offer you right now.” The next day, they told us that was the only room they could give us and that we could either take it or look for another hotel.

author: Akanshu J
title: Undisclosed Junk Amenity Fee + Retaliatory Charging After Negative Review
text:
I booked and prepaid the full advertised rate for my stay at NoMo SoHo through Booking.com. Nowhere in the booking confirmation or terms was any mandatory amenity, resort, or destination fee disclosed.

After checkout, the hotel charged my card an unauthorized amenity fee of $376.11. They refunded this amount on April 18, 2026. However, on April 19 they charged me again for $345.45 — the exact same type of fee.

On April 25, I called the hotel and spoke directly with the Director of Revenue. she openly admitted that the second charge was made because I had left a negative Google review about how the hotel handled the first unauthorized fee. The Director told me to “take the money from Booking.com” and then abruptly ended the call.
Despite sending all proof multiple times to both the hotel and Booking.com, I have received zero replies or resolution as of April 28.

This is a clear case of an undisclosed junk fee combined with retaliatory billing. Extremely unprofessional and disappointing.
I strongly recommend other travellers choose a different hotel.

author: glasgowgals
title: Still the best!
text:
Having visited this accommodation many years ago. I knew what to expect and as always it hit the mark.
The room was  big  and comfy, air con , great wardrobe and storage , fab shower and a wee fridge too it was ideal.
Wi-Fi connectivity was brilliant too.
The location is in a great district. Lots of facilities around the corner. 
And a stroll to the Vatican and Castel Angelo.

Luca and his son are charming and helpful hosts. 
Our taxi he arranged to the airport was superb, prompt service lovely car. Driven by Roberta.

We will be back. Ciao !

author: Sarah B
title: 10 out of 5 stars
text: We had an absolutely wonderful stay at Rome Armony Suites. The room we stayed in was a large family room which was cleaned daily and had bottled water left each day which was very kind. We travelled as a family and found it a safe, lovely area to stay in, so close to all the major tourist sites that we walked to the Vatican and used the subway for further travels with no issues. Luca was an exceptional host who helped us with everything. He gave us assistance in finding allergy friendly and gluten free places to eat. He booked transfers for us to and from the airport and the drivers did a fantastic job. There was a massive traffic jam on the way to the airport and our driver went miles out of his way through countryside so we made our flight. Likewise, the breakfast place he booked for us each day was very convenient and we really liked it. We really loved our stay and cannot recommend it enough as a place to stay. Many many thanks !!

author: Domenic S
title: Luca is the Best!
text:
Luca is one of the nicest people I’ve ever met
Very detailed and cares deeply about your stay
Location is perfect. Very safe and quiet neighborhood 
About 15 min walk to Vatican, 50 min walk to coliseum, 30 min walk to piazza navona 
Room is clean and easy to rest in
If he offers the airport pickup, take it!  Mercedes Benz for reasonable rate 
Definitely will stay here again when I return to Rome

author: Tracy
title: Our new favorite hotel in Rome
text:
First let me say that I traveled internationally for most of my career and I have stayed in hundreds of 5 star hotels with tons of amenities. While this is not a 5 star hotel, Luca and his family provided the best customer service of any hotel I have ever experienced. His dedication to his clients is the best ever, bar none. The room was immaculately clean, well-appointed, with the biggest bed I have ever seen. The location is perfect; close enough to walk to the Vatican, the Spanish steps, and other famous attractions, but in a real neighborhood. It is the perfect balance for those who love to experience cities the way a local experiences them. 
Luca gave us suggestions for tours and attractions that we never would have considered but are delighted that he told us about. His restaurant recommendations were perfect. We had delicious food at great prices. We were there for a week and we will be coming back before we fly home. 
When I couldn’t figure out how to book a train ticket online (Italian train tickets  are clunky using  their website and hard to understand) Luca handled it all for me before I even arrived. His knowledge of the city and its attractions is invaluable and his patience and kindness are unparalleled. I told him that I had read a negative review and fell in love with him based upon his intelligent and hilarious response. Clearly the person writing that review was a jealous competitor. 
If the rating scale goes to 5 stars, this place is a solid 10. We feel like we have made a friend for life. If you are considering this hotel for your trip to Rome, book now. You will be elated that you made the right choice!

author: Marta
title: Stay by Luca!
text:
Staying with Luca was a pleasant surprise in the capital!
Highly recommended for services, room, location and especially for advice on what to see and where to eat!
The location is quiet convenient to the Vatican and Lepanto metro, the clean room with XXXL bed😄, spacious shower, bedroom slippers and bottle of water on the bedside table every day (much appreciated)
Thanks Luca!

author: catherine m
title: VERY GOOD HOTEL
text: Very welcoming staff, top-notch cleanliness, very varied breakfast, I recommend it 100% except unfortunately for the exterior which is not up to the hotel. GO THERE WITHOUT ANY PROBLEM.

author: BuffaloSteve
title: 5 Star Service, Location & Hospitality
text:
5-Star: 
Excellent Location, Outstanding Service, and True Marriott Hospitality

My wife and I recently spent a few days at the Element Times Square West during our visit to New York City, and the experience exceeded our expectations.

The location is hard to beat—just a short walk to Times Square, Madison Square Garden, Broadway theaters, restaurants, and multiple subway lines. It made exploring NYC incredibly easy without needing a taxi.

What truly stood out, however, was the service. Anjelita at the front desk was exceptional throughout our stay. We interacted with her several times, and she was consistently friendly, professional, knowledgeable, and eager to help. She made us feel genuinely welcome and was one of the highlights of our stay.

I would also like to recognize Brianna, the General Manager, for her outstanding hospitality. She took the time to assist us personally and arranged a thoughtful room upgrade that made our visit even more special. The communication and attention to guest satisfaction were evident throughout our stay and reflected positively on the entire team.

I should also note, John E in the breakfast area was exceptionally friendly and helpful. He even surprised my wife with hash browns that were not out that day and she mentioned she wanted some in passing… John E showed up at the table with some minutes later. Wow! Salamat, John! 

As a Lifetime Titanium Elite member with more than 2,000 nights at Marriott properties worldwide, I have stayed in many hotels over the years. What keeps me loyal to Marriott is the people, and the team at Element Times Square West exemplifies the hospitality that has made the brand successful.

Thank you to Anjelita, Brianna, and the entire staff for helping make our New York City trip such a memorable experience. We would gladly stay here again on a future visit.

One bonus tip for fellow travelers: If you’re a pizza lover, don’t miss the pizza shop directly across the street called Square Pizza. During our trip I sampled pizza from several well-known NYC locations, and surprisingly, my favorite slice was right there across from the hotel. The classic cheese slice was outstanding, and the garlic knots were the best I’ve ever had. We enjoyed it so much that we went back twice!

⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐

author: Mirlou
title: 3 day New York break
text: Lovely hotel, clean and tidy. Staff were very helpful and polite. Bathrooms were spacious and clean. Bedrooms were ideal size with very comfortable bed. Room had a hob cooker , full size fridge and dishwasher. Rooms were cleaned everyday. Breakfast was a buffet style with pancakes ,omelette ,scrambled eggs which Was lush , sausages and muffins to tea coffee and juices. Hotel is located close to Times Square probably about a 10 minute walk . I would definitely stay at this hotel again

author: Yabrinya T
title: GREAT LOCATION, PRICE AND VIEW!
text:
The location was perfect, short walk to Broadway/Times Square.  The price was reasonable and the view was AMAZING!  Extended stay with small kitchenete, full fridge, stovetop, microwave - save money on meals!  Higher floor (35) no noise and great view of the skyline.  Great HOT breakfast and evening Happy Hour (Beer/wine).  I never had any problem with the slow elevator.
Con - no drawers for my clothes, terrible lighting in the bathroom, no vanity or ledge in the shower to hold my stuff.
Overall, I would stay here again for the price and location, nothing fancy but more than suitable for a Broadway weekend!

author: kevinvalue
title: I'll definitely stay here again!
text:
Excellent Location. Just a block from the subway station. Quiet enough street despite being in the Times Square area. Great place to feel that New York City energy.
Clean room equipped with everything you could need, including fridge, dishwasher, stovetop, glassware, and cooking utensils. 
Excellent Value. 
Great breakfast buffet. 
Also, one of the better hotel gyms I've seen

Special shoutout to Damien at the Front Desk, he is amazing.

author: higgy5150
title: Would Definitely Return
text:
Had a most enjoyable stay with my teenage daughter last month; there for 5 nights.
Lovely room, quite spacious for NY, very comfortable beds, all that we needed.
Stayed on floor 33; had a little wait for the lifts but didn’t not experience too long a delay during our stay.
Excellent location away from Times Square, etc yet with good subway links close by.
Plenty going on in the vicinity.

author: Peter Hordijk
title: Good hotel for a short stay
text: Stayed at this hotel for two nights. Spacious room with King size bed. Bathroom with shower. No bath. There was no view. You were looking at a wall. Hotel is near Wallstreet, the 9-11 Memorial and Brooklin Bridge. All sights are easily accessible by metro.

author: Ruth C
title: NY Doubletree hilton
text: Rooms too small. Toliet wouldn't flush properly. Towels scratchy. No conditioner. Rude girl at elevators. Hard to get an elevator up or down. Grace at front desk was nice.

author: cordell13
title: Enjoyable stay
text: Loved our stay! Great location, clean comfortable rooms. Perfect for our trip to New York. Would stay here again!

author: Regina S
title: Decent choice is  you are coming without car
text:
We stayed as a couple mid March and wanted to explore the area for a few days
 Pros: 
Location- only if you are using public transportation or taxi/uber. Close to major attractions, shops, bars, food and subway stops
Clean hotel
Very nice view, booked river view king room and asked for higher floor
Staff was professional, very pleasant and made us feel welcome 
Luggage storage on the ground level
Sufficient breakfast that was included with our stay
Cons:
Location- if you are coming by car
Misleading info on website about self parking. 
No parking on site at all, was recommended a valet parking 2 blocks away(did not used)
Absolutely no place to unload the car. 
Cars parked multiple hours in front of the hotel, I.e. loading zone, and hotel does not enforce them to move. 
Reception in the second floor, which doesn’t make it easier to check in when you have luggage
 3 elevators , but only 2 worked most of the time
Bed is way smaller than king, I’m hardly over 5 feet, and if my head was down the pillow, then my feet stick out from the bed. 
Plus some minor issues, like safety deposit lock didn’t work, iron was not heating at all, tv channels didn’t work - for those we called reception and they tried to  resolve. 
In conclusion, if you are coming without car, want to  explore the area, it’s a  decent choice due to location  and cleanliness of the hotel. Make sure to leave the luggage downstairs, go up one floor for check in(stairs), then come back for your luggage and take the elevator. 
Higher floors are better than middle ones, at least we could catch an empty elevator.

author: JamesG_uk
title: Hit and miss and this once great hotel
text:
The Saint Pancras Renaissance Hotel used to be my go-to property in London but then the Great Northern appeared on the scene and I switched my allegiance.

Once GNH departed Marriott I gave the St. Pancras another chance as I posted previously in this forum (in April 2026).

I had been disappointed by the lack of upgrades as the years went by after previously scoring some magnificent suite upgrades.

During my last visit, I was pleased to see the Barlow wing renovation had been completed and the rooms have been brought up to a far more luxurious standard with beautiful bathrooms, nice furnishings in the hotel room itself and even great taste for carpet. The corridors had also been repainted and re-fitted in a moody dark blue colour.

Having been buoyed by my visit earlier in the year, I decided to stick the hotel on my list once again. However, even though I emailed the hotel ahead of time to remind them that I would be returning to the property, I’m afraid that the experience at this hotel is very much hit or miss.

The air-conditioning for starters is virtually non-existent and on one of the hottest days of the summer the temperature was unable to get below 25°C bracket (77F). This is unacceptable for a hotel charging upwards of £300 per night!

I was also not upgraded in any way shape or form having booked a loft room in the Barlow wing. I was given exactly that and my suite night award request was rejected.

Complaining after the first nights sleep I was moved to a room on a lower floor which was slightly larger and in which the air-conditioning was a little better (although never by meeting the exacting standards some people that require their bedrooms to be precooled.)

As far as furnishings in the hotel go it was a particularly pleasant place to spend three nights.

Breakfast was served in the downstairs lobby area and there was a decent choice of offerings of smoked salmon, meats, bread, and pastries, and fresh fruit. Various hot options are available on request from a breakfast menu. The food quality was decent and a good breakfast was enjoyed by all.

It’s such a shame that nothing has ever been done to The Chambers Club. The lounge appears to remain unused.

Overall the visit was fine but the fact that this remains such a curates egg makes me give pause as to whether I will continue to stay there in the future.

That being said, when I pointed out to the hotel staff that was not happy with certain things during the stay, they were quick to rectify and did switch us to a new room within minutes of complaining, so there is credit where it’s due.

author: cjmac59
title: Poor service and poor value
text: I have just left their terrace bar. After a lovely day in the city with my sister we decided to treat ourselves to a cocktail prior to going our separate ways. What a disappointment for me. My favourite cocktail by far is a Margarita  and I have never been served one without a salt rim however this is not the case at the St Pancras. I pointed it out to the waiter when I was served my drink but she bluffed that the salt was infused in my cocktail- it wasn’t   No one checked if we were happy and when it came to paying I mentioned it again. This waiter tried to fob me off with insisting it was a ‘ Heritage’ cocktail. I paid over £20 for my drink. I feel as an older lady the staff felt they could dismiss me and my concerns.

author: adeutsch2016
title: Great stay this time
text:
I have visited the hotel many times, this year alone 4, have made in the past many complains regarding some issues with laundry  etc. this time must say all went excellent, laundry, bar, breakfast, room. 
Would like to specially thank Mr. Yatharth (apologize if I  have written wrongly) who has been extremely efficient not only at quick check in (he understood I was tired after 15 hour flight) but next days helping with prints and other matters. It’s nice when you see that the hotel has improved service to guests. As a liftime Bonvoy  plat I travel a lot and not usual this days to see someone go beyond his obligations to solve guests problems. Thank you

author: DYLANESQUE2014
title: If you haven’t been to this hotel get in a car or train and go there now
text:
My wife and I had been in London so she could have hospital treatment. Our train was cancelled due to a major problem with overhead lines on the East Coast mainline. 
So we decided to stay here overnight and boy were we were pleased that we did.
The hotel is luxurious and the architecture is incredible. We were greeted with champagne and had a memorable meal in the hotel that night with our son.
A singer and guitarist were playing cool tunes in the restaurant as we arrived for dinner!
It was a wonderful change from hospitals!
But in the end it’s the little things that count.
The following morning my wife was still tender after surgery and I was having difficulty with our bags as we checked out for Kings Cross.
One of the very friendly staff near the check in desk, Ian, spotted our predicament and asked if he could help.
Not only did he carry our luggage to the entrance he asked to carry it to the station down some very steep steps!!
Real service and with a lovely smile!
Thanks for being so kind Ian!

author: Amy L
title: Bumpy start but great overall
text:
Overall a great experience but with a bit of a shaky start. It’s a beautiful hotel, the room was amazing and very spacious. Staff were friendly and very helpful. The Booking Office is amazing. It’s a great location if you are travelling. 

Just a few things though- We arrived at check in time and our room wasn’t ready. Our room was directly opposite the lift which is really not ideal as you bump into people the second you open the door. If you are in the Barlow rooms and want to go to the spa, you have to walk through the foyer where people are having drinks, checking in etc. to get there, so it can be uncomfortable to go in robes. The spa is just a small pool and steam room- probably a better experience if you’re doing a treatment too.

author: Gonul B
title: There is no one to speak to at the hotel.
text:
Accommodating a single family at the hotel shouldn't be this difficult.

They couldn't arrange a double room and a twin room on the same floor.
We asked for the alcohol to be removed from the room, but they didn't do it.

We wanted the rooms to be on the same floor—ideally next to each other—but they couldn't manage it, even though notes had been added when the booking was made a month in advance.
They are very indifferent.

author: Marge M
title: May Fair Hotel
text: Excellent hotel in a great location for site seeing. Minakshi greeted us upon arrival to the hotel and did her very best to expedite the process. She kept us informed on the room status and was warm and welcoming.

author: yvonnewelton
title: Wonderful study in fantastic location
text:
We had a fabulous stay at the Mayfair recently. The location is fantastic so close to everything we needed, theatres, art galleries and luxury shops.
The decor of the hotel is great and the room was large with a very modern bathroom.
The staff were so helpful especially Kita on reception and Darren on the concierge desk. It turned out they are both from my home county of Yorkshire so no wonder!!

author: Torrey D
title: The Mayfair Hotel
text: The Mayfair Hotel, London is my home away from home! I am there for 10-12 days per month and am always welcomed back like a family member by Prerna, Irina and others. It is this recognition and level of service that keeps me coming back!

author: Richard
title: Good stay at May Fair
text: Latif and Katherine provided excellent customer service. The hotel is well appointed and in a great location for the west end of London.

author: avarpali
title: Top notch experience!
text: Wonderful experience from start to finish, the rooms are beautiful, the food and drinks are top class, but it is the genuine service through and through that made the experience outstanding. Thank you

author: Lorna
title: Great hotel in a great location!
text:
This is a great hotel, with caring staff and and is in a superb location. 
We stayed for 2 nights on 15th August . 
We received fantastic service from Jayson on arrival, he is genuinely kind and really showed care for us. 
The breakfast was very good and the team are all friendly. 
Our room was beautiful, we had a family suite on the 5th floor and we would definitely ask for that the next time we stay. 
And finally, we want to mention Zubin the front of house manager, he is fantastic, really professional and genuinely kind.

author: Sightsee45063930620
title: A LOVELY STAY IN THE HEART OF LONDON
text:
Following on from a recent stay at the Radisson Blu Bloomsbury Street Hotel in London, I wanted to share what a lovely experience we had. From the moment we arrived, everything was exactly as you would hope, and I genuinely haven’t got a bad word to say about the hotel.

Our room was a really good size, spotlessly clean and fresh, with a great shower. The soundproofing was excellent too – we didn’t hear any noise at all, which is always a big plus when staying in central London.

Every member of staff we dealt with, whether at reception, at breakfast or in the bar, was friendly, efficient and really helpful. Nothing seemed too much trouble and everything was handled professionally and with a smile.

The location is excellent too, just a short walk from Tottenham Court Road and right in the heart of London, making it a great base for enjoying everything the city has to offer.

author: Rhiannon Stanley
title: Nice stay for a theatre trip
text: Stayed here for one night for a theatre visit in the West End. The hotel/bar is really nice and staff were friendly and helpful. The room is spacious with a comfortable bed I have marked down as the air-con was faulty and it was a very hot night so didn't sleep too well. Apart from that it is a great place to stay and the location is excellent for theatre.

author: Lex
title: FABULOUS
text:
What a fabulous hotel. The moment we walked in the door to the moment we left, we were made to feel welcome and special. Hotel was spotlessly clean, staff were polite and very helpful, room was beautifully furnished and the breakfast was very tasty. Eggs ordered freshly cooked to your liking (scrambled eggs were on the buffet for those that didn't want to wait)
Very well situated. walking distance to Oxford Street and Covent Garden.
We will definitely be returning guests.
Thank you to the entire Team for making our stay perfect.

author: NATASHA N
title: My stay at Le Bristol made my anniversary truly unforgettable.
text:
I had visited Le Bristol many times before for its wonderful restaurants, but this time, for my birthday, I finally had the pleasure of staying for three nights in a beautiful room with a balcony overlooking the Eiffel Tower.

From beginning to end, the experience was exceptional. The hospitality was warm, polished, and highly professional, the food was consistently outstanding, and the cleanliness and overall condition of the hotel were impeccable. The only purely personal preference I might mention is that I would have enjoyed a slightly firmer bed, but aside from that, I truly have no complaints.

What made the stay especially memorable were the thoughtful little surprises each day. On my birthday, knowing how much I love animals, the team even arranged for me to spend a moment holding the hotel’s beloved cat, which was such a touching and unforgettable gesture.

Even when I made special requests on my birthday, the staff never made me feel that anything was too much trouble. They handled everything with grace, kindness, and genuine professionalism, always trying to make the experience as special as possible.

Thanks to everyone at Le Bristol, I was able to create truly beautiful memories that I will always cherish. It was an unforgettable birthday stay, and I already look forward to returning again very soon.

author: Cosmo P
title: Beautiful Weekend at Le Bristol
text: I had the most incredible stay at Le Bristol recently.Nothing is too much for the team.The food is great, the concierge were so attentive and the service was on another level.It totally elevated our experience in Paris.I will definitely stay here again.

author: Kiran Robinson
title: Celebrating the centennial of Le Bristol Paris
text: Lunch at Café Antonia Le Jardin Français is an invitation to experience an uncompromising celebratory meal. The menu unfolds through an inspired selection of vibrant salads, pure earth driven unadulterated flavors. Delicate appetizers, phenomenal signature dishes and supreme desserts tailored with fastidious precision to detail. Paired with masterfully culled Champagne anthology and an invitation to explore their exhaustive global wine anthology. Every element comes across together to create an unforgettable expression of French art de vire!

author: Theresa
title: Perfect birthday stay
text:

Everything about the hotel feels luxurious, but because it’s so small and intimate, it has this wonderful boutique, almost private members’ club feel rather than a typical London hotel.

They really have thought of everything — there are treats available all day, scones with jam in the afternoon, canapés between 5pm and 7pm, and even a hot dish later in the evening. author: John S
title: Hotel 41 absolutely lives up to the reviewsHotel 41 absolutely lives up to the reviews
text:
I just returned from a quick trip to London at the end of a longer vacation and stayed at Hotel 41 for 2 nights. I've been traveling to London for more than 30 years, from when I was much younger and broke to many business trips and, more recently, staying at some much nicer hotels. I've stayed all over the city and definitely have my favorites, so I'm surprised I'd never heard of Hotel 41 before.

I chose it mainly because we were arriving at Gatwick and the location near Victoria Station made it very convenient. I was also intrigued by the incredible reviews. I knew the Rubens next door, but had never stayed there, so I watched a few YouTube videos about Hotel 41 before booking and it looked like a very unique experience.

From the moment we arrived, I understood the reviews. Check-in takes place upstairs in the lounge and it immediately felt like we were being welcomed into a private club. This was also my first introduction to the level of service here. I've stayed at many 5 star hotels around the world including Four Seasons, Ritz-Carlton, Okura and Taj properties, and Hotel 41 had some of the best service I've ever experienced.

What makes the service so impressive is that it isn't pretentious at all. Everyone seemed genuinely interested in taking care of anything we needed, but at the same time they were incredibly friendly and approachable. It almost felt like being taken care of by friends. I've never seen a hotel balance impeccable service with that level of warmth quite this well.

Our room was small, but that's typical for London, and there was an incredible amount of attention to detail throughout the room. We even had a view toward the Buckingham Palace Mews. I also have to mention the air conditioning! As an American who struggles with European AC in the summer, I've learned which London hotels have good air conditioning. Hotel 41 has officially set a new standard. The room could get VERY cold. There were actually times I had to turn the temperature up, which is something I don't think I've ever said during a summer trip to London.

My only minor criticism of the room was the shower, which was extremely small. It was difficult to shower without constantly being under the water. In the hotel's defense, there was also a shower over the bathtub that I could have used. Given the age and design of many London buildings, I understand they have to work with the space available.

The service continued to impress throughout our stay. The lounge really does feel like a private club and we had a great breakfast there. Housekeeping was also exceptional. One day I worked from the room for most of the day and assumed we'd missed the cleaning window. I mentioned that we'd only be leaving later for dinner and was genuinely surprised to return to a completely cleaned room. Even the little details impressed me, like neatly organizing and tying up my power cords.

I really can't say enough good things about Hotel 41. Unfortunately, it's a little outside what I can spend on my business trips, but for personal trips this has officially become my new favorite hotel in London. After more than 30 years of staying at hotels throughout the city, that's saying a lot.  I actually hesitated a bit in writing this review because I'm worried as more people discover this property the rates will increase significantly.  I almost want to keep this hotel a secret!  Ha!  But as a frequent traveler and hotel snob, I must give Hotel 41 credit where it is due.

author: Luc van der Linden
title: A Truly Memorable Solo Stay in London
text:
I had an excellent stay at Hotel 41. Even before my arrival, the team were incredibly helpful in answering my questions and ensuring everything was arranged for a smooth visit.
The room was spotless, and I especially appreciated the evening turndown service. The boutique layout, with the Executive Lounge at the heart of the hotel, created a welcoming and relaxing atmosphere where it was easy to enjoy breakfast or simply unwind.
What really made the stay special was the service. Several members of the team recognised me by name, there was always someone at the entrance to welcome me back or help arrange a taxi, and everyone took a genuine interest in how my day had been. One member of staff even prepared a personalised list of recommendations for me to read over while I was having breakfast.
The location may not be ideal for everyone, particularly if your main focus is Soho, Covent Garden or the City of London. However, for exploring Westminster, Buckingham Palace, St James's, Belgravia and Mayfair, I found it excellent. Although some destinations are a little farther away, there was always a member of staff available to arrange a taxi, making it incredibly easy to get anywhere in London.
Hotel 41 exceeded my expectations in every respect, and I hope to return on a future visit to London.

title: luxury
text:
Rome Cavalieri Hotel: A jewel of luxury and enchanting view
​The Rome Cavalieri, A Waldorf Astoria Hotel stands as a luxurious landmark perched atop Monte Mario hill, offering its guests an unparalleled panoramic view of the historic city of Rome and its timeless landmarks such as St. Peter's Basilica.
​An exceptional stay experience
​The hotel is set on a vast expanse of lush Mediterranean gardens, giving it an atmosphere of privacy and tranquility away from the hustle and bustle of the city center, while maintaining easy access to Rome’s most prominent neighborhoods.
​Key Features and Services
​Upscale restaurants: The hotel includes the renowned La Pergola restaurant, which has three Michelin stars, offering a world-class dining experience under the supervision of the most famous chefs.
​Art Museum: The hotel is a living art gallery, housing a private and unique collection of paintings, artworks, historical artifacts and tapestry sculptures that adorn its lobbies and rooms.
​Spa and relaxation: The hotel offers a fully equipped spa center, ranked among the best in Europe, with indoor and outdoor swimming pools, fitness centers, and tennis courts.
​The Rome Cavalieri is an ideal destination for travelers seeking to combine the grandeur of Italian history with the highest levels of luxury and modern hotel service.
