author: TheOrchards
title: Beware if you have a dietary intolerance or allergy
text: Some aspects of our stay were very good other aspects seriously poor. I've given an average rating to reflect the seriousness of the lack of understanding with regard to dietary intolerances. We had a very warm welcome on arrival and our twin room was spacious and comfortable with good mattresses though hard and a very good bathroom. Robes and slippers were provided. However one of the twin beds had a headboard and the other shared part of that headboard but the rest of the bed was against the wall so it was uncomfortable when sitting up in bed (see photo)! We had made it clear in an email when booking and at check in that we had a gluten intolerance and asked for gluten free biscuits and oat milk to be put in the room. Neither were provided BUT biscuits containing gluten were in our room. We asked for the oat milk so a member of staff came to our room to deliver it at which time I asked if the biscuits in the room were gluten free. She didn't know, said she would enquire and bring gluten-free ones if they were not. We went out at that point and returned to find a new plate of biscuits in our room which we of course thought were the new gluten-free ones. We both had a bite and I said to my sister "don't eat any more (I spat mine out) I suspect they contain gluten". I phoned reception and she asked me to describe the biscuits. I did and she said that they were normal gluten containing biscuits!!!! I was very annoyed but polite and she was very unaware and unhelpful so I asked for a manager. Declan the manager on duty was lovely and apologetic and said that he would be furious if such a thing had happened to him. He looked after us at dinner which was an excellent meal and he didn't charge us for drinks or dessert as a gesture which we appreciated. We felt that all would go well after that. At breakfast we told the staff that we were gluten free and all went well. No biscuits appeared in our room on the second day - we didn't mind. At breakfast the second day we again reminded them that we were gluten free BUT unbelievably my sister was served her boiled egg with gluten containg soldiers - how is that even possible!!! They had already given us gluten free toast! As the soldiers looked like different bread to the gluten-free toast and because I didn't trust them I asked if the soldiers were gluten-free and we were taken aback when the waitress said "oh no they're not sorry about that" and didn't take my sister's plate but instead grabbed the soldiers in a handful and took them off her plate!! Unbelievable! We were in a hurry to leave and catch our train so didn't talk to a manager. Check out was good. Most of the staff were lovely, especially the young man on reception and the man who showed us to our room and around the hotel on arrival and of course Declan who was brilliant. However a thoroughly unpleasant woman on reception was handling a complaint from a tall guest who was complaining about the ceiling height in his room. As well as seemingly being unable to apologise to him and making him annoyed in her approach, when he had gone she proceeded to say unpleasant things about him whilst we sat just feet away. It was extremely unprofessional and rude. The staff really need to be trained about the vital importance of dietary intolerances and allergies as they clearly don't understand the seriousness of such matters.

author: Stuart P
title: Not great!
text:
This is a pretty ropey hotel. I just wish I had looked at trip advisor first before booking.
The location is great I have to say, some nice places to eat literally just outside the hotel, including a great coffee house. Tube station a 2 or 3 min walk and the high St less than that. That's where the good points end unfortunately. There is no breakfast or food available in the hotel (I was told this on arrival) so a lot of the stuff you see on booking websites is false. The hotel is really run down, loads of repair work needed, everywhere you look there are bodged repairs. My room was like a furnace as there is no AC. Impossible to sleep in the current summer heat. Lots of homeless people sleeping rough near the hotel and plenty of shady people walking around. To be honest London is getting worse week by week, its a proper grotty city these days and reminds me a lot of the the big US city's where poverty is hidden just a street or two back from the main tourist areas and business districts. 
The staff are friendly enough and the rooms were clean so I cant really blame them for the hotels main misgivings.
Massively overpriced for the a three star hotel. Even based on the location £80 a night would be a fair price to pay.

author: Vera S
title: Unsafe
text: We stayed two nights at this hotel. We had checked into our room on the ground floor and then went straight into town. In the evening we came back. When I pulled up the curtain there was a homeless man AGAINST our window doing drugs. There were also five other people next to our window, who made a lot of noise. author: GrandTour66900328188
title: Misleading Photos, Poor Service, and an Extremely Disappointing StayA
text:
Our experience at Cheshire Hotel was extremely disappointing from start to finish.

The hotel bears very little resemblance to the photos used to advertise it. The rooms we received were of a much lower standard than expected, outdated, poorly maintained, and completely different from what was shown online. We chose this hotel based on the advertised images, and the reality was nowhere close.

The customer service made the situation even worse. The reception staff were dismissive, unhelpful, and unwilling to understand or address our concerns. Rather than trying to resolve the issue, they insisted that we pay extra for an "upgrade." The upgraded room was nothing special—a small room with a basic double bed—yet we were charged a total of **£470**, which was completely unreasonable for what was offered.

The payment process for the upgrade was also highly concerning. Instead of providing a secure payment link or accepting a bank transfer, we were asked to provide our credit card details over the phone. This felt unprofessional and did not inspire confidence.

Throughout our stay, the staff were rude, dismissive, and made us feel like our concerns did not matter. Instead of acknowledging that the rooms did not match the advertised standard, they simply refused to help.

This was one of the worst hotel experiences we have had. author: Mr C
title: Please consider another hotel
text:
I booked a room with a kitchenette (Studio) on check in I was handed a piece of papers which said cooking was not allowed in the room. Despite it having the microwave and freezer there were no plates or cutlery. They also asked to scan my ID, this is not permitted for UK residents in a UK hotel. 

Once in the room I found evidence of bed bugs in the mattress. I was then moved to another room where the extractor was so loud and again no way to cook or eat in the kitchenette. I was then moved to a third smaller room where the wall paper and the door frame had been tapped up. The door was also already open as we approached.

The receptionist knocked the door again, offering a room change. This would have been the fourth change.

I contacted the hotel with my concerns who responded with. Cooking is not allowed due to fire risks, this suggests the rooms are not fit for purpose and are a fire risk and that the photos do not match their room and appear to be old. 

This means that they were selling rooms that could not be used as their intended purpose a breach of the customer rights act 2015 "A kitchen that cannot be used for cooking is a facility that is "unfit for purpose." 

As well as Consumer Protection from Unfair Trading Regulations 2008 which prohibits "Misleading Actions" and "Bait and Switch" tactics.

Advertising a room with a "kitchenette" implies it is a facility you can use to prepare food. By banning cooking after you paid, they misled you into a contract under false pretences. 

There also also signs staying that if you do not request a safe of give valuables to a manager then items (in rooms) are left at own risk as well as signs with hand sanitizer for covid - 19

These concerns have now been passed on to the council and health and safety for investigation

author: caroline p
title: A nice address but a few details to review!
text:
We are currently staying at the Chesterfield Mayfair and our first impression is rather positive. The room is clean, quiet, and well-designed in terms of storage. The bedding is also very comfortable, which is obviously appreciated after a day in London.
A few points disappointed us, however. The bathroom is quite small and, unfortunately, there is no walk-in shower: it is a bathtub equipped with a non-slip shower mat. It is not very practical and, in an establishment of this standing, we would have appreciated a more modern installation.
The room is also a bit dark and would deserve to be refreshed. The furniture is very well made, but some of it is damaged, and a stained chair unfortunately gives an impression of a lack of maintenance. It’s a shame, because the potential is really there.
Breakfast was also a source of misunderstanding. A menu in the room indicates two prices for us: £25 for the continental breakfast and £30 for the English breakfast. But this morning, once we went down to the restaurant, another menu was given to us, with different prices. This difference between the information in the room and that of the restaurant is quite surprising and deserves to be clarified.
Finally, the staff is very professional, smiling, and respectful, which is a real positive point. We simply regretted that some members of the team did not take more time to speak more slowly with guests who do not perfectly master the language of Shakespeare. A little more patience and adaptation would make the experience even more pleasant.
In summary: a hotel that has many assets—location, quiet, comfortable bedding, and professional staff—but which, in our opinion, deserves some improvements and more consistency in the services offered. At this level of quality, these small details make all the difference.

title: A Wonderful Stay at The Chesterfield Hotel Mayfair
text:
We chose The Chesterfield for a birthday celebration and it surpassed every expectation.

Set right in the heart of Mayfair, the location is unbeatable — close to all of London's best offerings, yet peaceful enough to escape the bustle.

The hotel is warm and inviting from the second you walk through the door, striking that rare balance between refined and relaxed.

We booked the junior suite to mark the birthday, and the team went the extra mile — cards and a cake were waiting in the room when we arrived. It was such a sweet, personal gesture that made the celebration feel truly memorable.

Every inch of the room and the wider hotel was pristine.

Even with Mayfair buzzing just outside, the room stayed remarkably peaceful — hardly a sound made it through.

The service was faultless. From arrival to departure, every member of staff was warm, attentive, and quick to help. The restaurant team especially stood out, guiding us through the menu with great recommendations.

A definite highlight was the rooftop bar, perfect for unwinding on a balmy summer evening.

All in all, this was a fantastic stay, and one we'd love to repeat. We'd wholeheartedly recommend it to anyone after a luxurious escape paired with genuinely attentive service.

title: The worst hotels I've ever had in London.
text:
Booked and paid for Standard Room, 19 m2. In fact, at the time of settlement got a 10 m2 kamorka category Single, half of what he paid for. When I pointed it out at the reception, I started openly claiming that I was wrong, that this was the number that was declared, until I showed the pictures with the real dimensions.

After that, I was "transferred" first to a room on the ground floor with windows that do not open at all and do not know where, then to another room, which turned out to be only 15 m2. I mean, I've been moved in three times and never given what I actually paid for.

And now for the condition of the rooms themselves: no air conditioning, no fan, the fridge covered in chips and scratches, like I've been in an accident, the drawers of nightstands and chests of drawers falling off or completely broken, the walls stained with black divorces and scratched, and at the end they gave me torn towels - as if that were normal.

Breakfast, which in a Booking.com photo looked varied, in reality turned out to be a couple of scarce hot dishes, one kind of sausage, one kind of cheese, three kinds of fruit and cereal with milk. OK.

As if that weren't enough - the floor is undergoing a full renovation: drill, hammer, workers constantly walking down the hall. There was no mention of this on the hotel's website, Booking.com or check-in.

I approached the front desk with each problem separately, repeatedly, and each time I got a denial - even when I showed the photos as direct evidence. No one was solving anything or helping.

For that kind of money and the four stars you're claiming, it's a real horror. Don't believe the photos on the site, the reality turned out to be completely different.

author: Chris M
title: Paying for the name, not the quality
text:
Very disappointed with my recent stay, as the title mentions, your very much paying for the Name of the hotel rather then the quality of it in itself . 

The negatives first, 

The hotel is extremely old and outdated. There’s zero question about that. The external entrance to the hotel needs a new lease of life as is looking a bit drab. The main foyer itself is nice, clean, tidy etc, spacious etc, but the problems creep up once past that point. 

The Room - Deluxe Family Room
Upon entering our room, we were without the complimentary free water, no slippers or robes etc. Took over an hour for these to be brought up too after requesting them, and when they were, slippers nor the Robs fit myself at all. Not the best start. 

The room itself, whilst nice enough, was not what I would expect a ‘Marriot’ room to be. There were large coffee stains on the floor by the bed, other food / drink stains splattered about on the carpet,  scratched and peeling mirror in the bathroom, artwork that had clearly gotten wet and stained at some point and pen scribbles on the base of one of the beds. Also, no lock on the bathroom door, seemingly broken and never replaced which seemed odd. 

The Rooms Balcony - 
The balcony, whilst great to have some outside space and access to fresh air which is a huge plus, was again, extremely tired and outdated. The tiny space we did have overlooked the car park and bins, so the view was awful and we were interrupted constantly during the night by car alarms, people slamming car doors etc. The railings were rust stained and not recently cleaned, same too for the air conditioning vents, and the external floor of the balcony. 

We did not use the gym, sauna etc whilst there, but did use the pool. 

2 parts to this, 1) it was great to have access to a swimming pool and nice to be able to take the kids swimming on site, BUT having worked in leisure industry for years: this pool and the changing room facilities etc are TIRED and hugely outdated. Half the lockers in the changing rooms were out of battery, general decor was extremely drab and worse then many budget gyms and health centres. The pool itself was stuffy, only 1.2m deep at its deepest and the tiles and surrounding area were dull, poorly decorated and simply 20 years too old without an update 

The corridors to the rooms were also seemingly never touched as just a door down to us there was a Nando’s delivery bag left in the corridor that was there from when we checked in, to the afternoon the next day when we checked out. This wasn’t the only lot of rubbish left outside doors that seemingly was never collected. 

On to the positives: 

We ate dinner at the Hotel restaurant and have to say the staff were very polite and welcoming, and the food was great, not excessively expensive either so can’t have many complaints there. That was an overall positive experience. 

Breakfast was included in the room price and again, have to say, very nice, lost of selection for just about anything you could want and was offered by staff to make anything we wanted that wasn’t on the buffet so again, very helpful and positive interactions there. 

Overall, my overarching feeling is we’ve left with more negatives then positives and have stayed in lesser name hotels for a lot less financially and come away with much better reviews and feelings on it, 

Based on the negatives, and that I don’t see the necessary updates being made anytime soon, I would not recommend the Hotel to friends and family.

author: adinj
title: Avoid this Marriott, it’s a motel, with no basic HYGIENE, no POWER BACK UP, NO WATER through the  day, NO ELEVATOR OPERA
text: This is a hotel I would strongly recommend avoiding. Despite paying over £300 per night and being a Marriott Platinum Elite member, my stay was plagued by a continuous lack of basic services and facilities. Most hotel services appear to be outsourced, and the result is an unacceptable level of service. Throughout my stay, room cleaning was inconsistent or absent, rubbish was not cleared, water was not replenished, laundry requests were ignored, and issues with air conditioning and drainage remained unresolved despite multiple complaints to reception staff and the housekeeping manager. Even simple requests, such as drinking water, often took more than two hours to be fulfilled. Repeated complaints resulted in little action and no meaningful resolution. The situation reached its worst when the hotel experienced a power and water outage for an entire day. Guests were given little to no information, there appeared to be no effective backup arrangements, and we were left climbing five flights of stairs repeatedly. There was no access to functioning washrooms, no drinking water from the taps, and no replenished bottled water in rooms. While operational issues can occur at any hotel, what was most disappointing was the response from management. After raising these concerns with a senior manager, the explanation provided was simply that these were “circumstances.” That response is wholly inadequate for a premium hotel charging these rates and operating under the Marriott brand. For a hotel positioning itself as an upscale property, one should at the very least expect basic hygiene, functioning facilities, clear communication during service disruptions, and responsive customer service. Unfortunately, my experience fell far below those expectations. The lack of accountability and the poor management response were the most disappointing aspects of an already unacceptable stay.

author: Daydream49764408592
title: Toxic Work Environment
text:
I wouldn’t recommend working for Travelodge based on my experience. The managers often seemed to be on power trips and set unrealistic expectations, particularly when it came to the number of rooms you were expected to clean between 10am and 2pm. Being expected to clean 17 rooms within that timeframe felt unreasonable, especially when management would simply tell you to “hurry up” multiple times and “clean faster” rather than offering any support.

There was also an instance where a staff member was expected to work both a morning and a night shift on the same day, which I found concerning and would question whether it was appropriate and even legal. There needs to be an investigation that goes on in that place. Another issue was the way staff were treated when making small mistakes. Something as minor as putting a cup in the wrong position or forgetting to replace a coffee could result in staff being made to feel demoralised rather than being given constructive feedback.

Communication with reception was another major problem. On numerous occasions, staff would try to call reception to report that they were unable to attend a shift, but the phone often wouldn’t be answered. Despite this, managers would tell staff to keep calling, even when there was clearly nobody answering. Also would put in the work groupchat a indirect message about to call the reception instead of messaging the number.

Overall, I found the management style stressful and unsupportive, with unrealistic workloads and poor communication. Based on my experience, I would think carefully before considering a job with Travelodge.

text:
My daughter had bought a gift voucher for afternoon tea at the Marriott Hotel, Marble Arch. Occasionally when we have redeemed a voucher we have been sat at the back of the restaurant and not been treated so well. 
Not today. 
From the moment we arrived Vivian, our host treated us like royalty. 
He was attentive but not overbearing. He remembered our names and recommended the best tea blends to go with our sandwiches and cakes.
The afternoon tea itself was dainty, exquisite and delicious. 
 Every member of staff was polite, warm and friendly. 
It was a wonderful experience and we will definitely go again for special family occasions.

author: ameliatravellifes
title: the best hotel
text:
As always, Marriott did not disappoint. I'm a loyal Marriott guest, and this hotel once again delivered excellent service, comfortable rooms, and a welcoming atmosphere.

The staff were friendly and professional, the room was spotless, and the location was perfect for exploring London. Everything was smooth from check-in to check-out.

I always enjoy staying with Marriott, and I look forward to my next visit. Highly recommended!

author: Haider A
title: Amazing Refurbishment
text: The location is unmatched, 5 minutes walk to the Hyde Park and Marble Arch. It’s newly refurbished and is in perfect condition. Heinrich at the front desk is an exceptional person. Greets everyone with a smile and makes you comfortable. My check in was done in less than 3 minutes and even though I was early, he immediately got a room for me. For a central London accommodation, this place is the best

author: Leevi U

author: DayTrip393827
title: Quality time with husband as a couple and sight seeing.

Absolutely love the location of this hotel and the atmosphere is very relaxing and tranquil. When we checked in it was a special suprise to find out that we had been chosen as guest of the day and our room was upgraded to the deluxe room which was great thoughly enjoyed our room it was so clean and the bed was so comfortable. 
Definitely value for money with breakfast included. 
The noise level was nice and quiet and relaxing.. 
Will definitely be staying here again it is our favourite hotel by far.

author: Laura M

author: Mary K
title: What a view!!

When we arrived we found that our room had been upgraded at no cost and what a view!! During our stay the staff were really wonderful and accommodating. The food was delicious and we were even given the use of a local swimming pool. The location really magical. Right in the center of London. The marinas behind the hotel are full of charming restaurants and cafes and beautiful boats. You could base a whole holiday from here or just pass through. Everything is very convenient. Thank you again to the wonderful staff for such a lovely stay!

author: Janet S

author: JONATHAN A

author: Colin D

author: rajesh n

author: Siddhant A

author: Andrea W

author: Wybos
title: Fantastic Hotel in a Perfect Location
text:
Stayed one night on 22 August with my daughter, we were celebrating a milestone birthday ( her 40th) and to see a show.
Understandably, the room wasn’t ready on arrival, the receptionist was very helpful and said they would call if it was ready early, so we left our bags and explored Covent Garden for lunch, the room was ready a little early, which was great, on arrival in the room, we were greeted with a bottle of Prosecco and chocolate cake with a birthday wish on the plate, it was a lovely surprise and really appreciated.
We stayed in a studio suite, which was nice and big, with a super king size bed and sofa that pulled out into a bed,the room was well appointed with plenty of sockets and a large bathroom with bath and separate shower , it was all very clean and plenty of towels. 
Plenty of tea and coffee facilities,  a complimentary mini bar and a jar of sweets which was a great touch.
We noticed that there wasn’t any bedding for the pull out bed, we called reception and it was sorted straight away.
We ate in Platform 7 restaurant in the evening, food and service was excellent and the waitress even presented a slice of cake and sung happy birthday, the bar served great cocktails which we just had to sample! 
Breakfast was excellent with plenty of choice 
 A fantastic stay in a fantastic hotel with great staff, perfect location for theatres and Covent Garden’s bars and restaurants.
Thoroughly recommend staying.
Thank you and we will be back .

author: angela l
title: Platform 7
text:
Lovely welcoming atmosphere 
Food is excellent . Great choice .
Beautifully decorated 
Could not ask for more in a relaxed pleasant atmosphere 
Jusu was an attentive server

author: Mabel K
title: Sister trip to UK
text: The Milestone is a wonderful place to stay in London. The service and staff are excellent. We had breakfast each day and it was good. We also highly recommend their high tea.

author: Reagan M
title: A must stay for a hotel snob
text: One of the most stunning, intentionally appointed, captivating hotels I have stayed in. Thoughtful staff, incredible location, delicious food, and the best hotel bar in the world. Most of London's best neighborhoods within walking distance, in a great area with quick access to cabs (which the wonderful doorman will hail on your behalf) and a tube station right around the corner. The rooms are all unique, and I am a total interior design snob so I was obsessed. The staff let thoughtful turndown service treats, everything was immaculate, and very spacious.

author: Katelyn S
title: Perfect tea time
text: Lovely experience! The atmosphere felt elegant and relaxing, the tea and pastries were delicious, and Akhil and Tim were both so friendly and welcoming.

author: Emily G
title: Fabulous
text: We had a lovely experience staying at the Milestone. We attended a concert at the Royal Albert Hall so it was very conveniently situated and made for an easy stroll there and back.  We were made to feel extremely welcome. All the staff are exceptionally friendly and nothing is too much trouble.  The room is beautifully decorated and very comfortable.  The spa, pool and gym are beautiful and as you book the space, completely private. We loved our stay and would definitely return.

author: Cathy A
title: Perfection at The Milestone
text: I can’t find enough words to describe our experience at the Milestone. It is a magnificent hotel in every way - the beauty,   our room, ambience,  comfort, service, food, housekeeping. Everyone was helpful, caring, warm. Alice, Dorina, Stephen, Victoria are a  few names we remember, but everyone was amazing. Thank you! The Milestone will definitely be our London hotel of choice in the future.

author: Patricia O
title: Excellent Location
text: Excellent location, comfortable and very good buffet breakfast. Spacious rooms and good heating. Totally recommended, I will definitely return.

author: Sean M
title: Ask for Keven
text: Stayed at the Hilton Olympia three nights and my guy Keven hooked me up every night at the society bar. I got the chance to talk to him during my last night and he is an amazing person, with a lot of interesting stories. If you have the opportunity to come here please ask for him because he will make your stay here in London more than worthwhile! Thank you again Keven! Wishing you all the best from the US.

author: Charlie T
title: Excellent stay + Value for Money
text:
Stayed just the one night at this hotel. Not entirely sure why it has such a low score, as we had an excellent stay. We had a late arrival and immediately the staff welcomed us and offered some water whilst checking in. The rooms are indeed dated, but they are exactly like the photos and are more than adequate and the premium rooms are an option where they have been renovated. There unfortunately was no gold upgrades as the hotel was busy, but the staff did check for this. The only pain was there was no plug sockets by the end which was a shame. No outside noise as we were on the 8th floor and also at the back of the hotel (most rooms face the back of the hotel).
However, the breakfast was exceptional, possible one of the best I have had across the Hilton group. The staff were super attentive, the offering was excellent, across both the hot and cold options.
Overall, for what is one of the cheapest Hilton’s consistently across London (often far cheaper than nearby Premier inn and travelodge), it has excellent service and a good night sleep. Would recommend.

author: Viscount Philip
title: Thank you so much
text:
Simply the best Hilton Hotel in London - As a Hilton Diamond Honors Member I have stayed at this hotel many times over the last few years. It offers excellent value for money; the rooms are clean and spacious; the breakfast is best of class; the staff friendly and welcoming. A few special mentions - Francesca (charming and lovely), the reception team (fantastic and helpful); the breakfast team (amazing and efficient - including the lovely waiter who gets my second cup of coffee); the bar team (very hard working and well looked after during the Diamond Happy Hours). Let’s hope that when the hotel does get a refurb none of its fine charm is lost.

Thank you for always looking after me.

author: Rory D
title: Excellent Staff

I always look forward to coming to this hotel as they really make the difference between a faceless service and an enjoyable experience.

author: cb

author: holidayheaven

author: Joe B

author: Adam W
title: Calm place to stay with very helpful staff
text:
Hitel provides a calm and peaceful place to stay when visiting Rome. The pool is great for cooling down after a day of walking and sight seeing. 

Staff are great, cheerful and alway happy to help. Variety and quality of Breakfast was very good. 

We opted for two family rooms with joining door. Both the rooms and bathrooms were spacious and kept very clean each day by staff which was great. 

The hotel is a 10min bus ride from the city centre and there are bus stops right outside the hotel making travel easy. Taxis can be booked using the 'free now' app and always arrived very quickly as well.

author: Santi V
title: Very good hotel with very attentive staff!

author: 44Kate
title: Fantastic hotel highly recommend
text:
Just returned from a 5 night stay , can  not fault this hotel at all . Staff were amazing hotel was excellent.  We booked through on the beach . I emailed the hotel direct a few weeks prior to see if they they offered airport transfer and they did , Maria was absolutely brilliant on the email arranging this , we had private transfer and Maurizto messaged me to say he was waiting outside and was brilliant. Only took about 30 mins and cost euro 65 . Hotel also arranged from transfer  back too . ( if you are on early flight they will also do you a breakfast bag to go which was brilliant too ) 
Our room
Was lovely king size bed and large sofa bed converted into bed ( teenager said bed was very comfy ) there is a fridge in room which was great and coffee machine , there is also a safe , steam
Iron and in our room couple of the sockets had usb ports , air con 
Shower  lovely and had shampoo and shower gel , we had email from hotel checking how we were settling in and just asking on feedback to which I just said could of done with more coffee pods and coat handles the next day knockOn door with all
Of this ! How amazing service !
Breakfast lovely served 7am -10am and lovely can’t fault it . Swimming pool absolutely brilliant and so happy to booked hotel with pool as was 40deg so was lovely to come back and co
Off , also had a pool day and chilled round the pool and had light snacks and drinks . They serve snack food until 9pm in hotel and drink until 11pm nice seating and lighting outside  
About 15 min walk to metro ( turn left outside hotel up to top of road and turn left all way down there ( just passed mc Donald’s ) also some other shop up there to to get your bus pass ( one with t outside) bus tickets includes metro too eur 150 for 100 min ( remember if on bus you must tap it to validate it ) bus conductors do get on we had one on ours ) there is bus stop outside takes you to city and we also went to trastervere  too ( took 2 stops)  
. We also walked to Vatican took approx 40 mins not ideal in heat but did it early morning . Metro is by far east but if you don’t fancy walk you have bus option outside . 
Lovely restaurant just 3mins down road called Ristorante Arturo turn right outside hotel ( shut on Mondays ) , it’s just before Crown  plaza hotel which is also has a restaurant you can go to too. We also walked past crown plaza to end of road At lights  then turned right and about another 5 min walk and found little sushi bar called nana sushi we had take out and took it back to room ( caught the bus back ) few other little restaurants there and then carry on walking up there is a little fair little ones on right hand side ( just past pharmacy)
We booked a lot of our trips with get your guide and never had any issues . 
Hope this of help . ( dont forgot water bottles to  fill up as lots of water fountains in the city. )

author: Crisentha V

author: Emma M
title: Disappointing Stay
text:
We had a mixed experience with our stay. While the hotel is advertised as 5-star, unfortunately the room itself didn’t feel like a 5-star experience. The furniture and decor felt very dated, there was no full-length mirror, only one bathrobe was provided despite the room being booked for two people, and the TV was positioned facing away from the bed. The air conditioning was also poor as it was located at the opposite end of the room than the bed, which wasn’t ideal for a London heatwave. Also please be aware the hotel is at least a 10 minute walk from any public transport if that’s something you need. 

The staff were generally friendly and pleasant. However, we had an issue at check-in and were essentially told that we needed to contact the booking agent ourselves to resolve it. We were left to deal with the situation on our own, which wasn’t the level of service we expected. We’re still not entirely sure whether the issue was the hotel’s or the booking agent’s fault, but we felt the hotel could have done more to assist us at the time as it was really stressful. 

There were also some disappointing issues with the food. At dinner, we found a large hair in one of our meals, which understandably put us off. Breakfast was generally fine, although on one morning we were told that they had already run out of one of the breakfast items by around 9am.

Overall, the staff were friendly (particular recognition to the front door staff and restaurant waiters), but the combination of the dated room, lack of attention to detail, food issue and the handling of our check-in problem meant that the experience fell short of what we would expect from a 5-star hotel. Personally we wouldn’t recommend the hotel and wouldn’t return.

author: Ale S
title: If you know them you avoid them. A nightmare.
text:
I swear if I could put zero stars on this "place," because it doesn't deserve to be called a hotel, I would put them on. Upon our arrival it seemed to me to have entered a nightmare, the room was in a basement, the stairs to go down were all covered with plastic, until you get to room n. 25 in which we were placed: the floor at our entrance was dirty, full of dust and hair (something reported and for which no solution was found), the walls of the room peeled and with moisture seepage, the bathroom sink is smaller than a goldfish tank, the shower dirty and malfunctioning (hot water practically absent). author: Nadeem A
title: Overall, we had a good family stay
text:
Overall, we had a good family stay and would like to thank Rahul, Waqas, Maria, and the housekeeping team for their kindness and assistance. The housekeeping lady was polite.
However, as an Accor Gold member, I was disappointed that no room upgrade was offered or even discussed during our 11-night stay. I would have expected my loyalty status to be recognized.
I would also like to highlight the following concerns:
Cleanliness: The room and ceiling areas were dusty. The area underneath the minibar/fridge was extremely dusty. I informed a team member and showed a photo, but it was never cleaned. Some bed linen was also old and had visible marks.
7th-floor ice machine: The ice machine was out of order throughout our stay, which was inconvenient.
Restaurant service: We had dinner at the all-day dining restaurant on our first night and paid cash. Service was not very attentive, and one pregnant staff member was particularly rude.
Bar service: The Mirror Bar staff were friendly, but some appeared to be trainees and lacked sufficient product/service knowledge.

Drink vouchers: Because we accepted alternate-day housekeeping, complimentary drink vouchers were offered. However, cocktails were refused when requested, and my son was also refused a milkshake. The voucher conditions should have been explained clearly.

Overall experience: I understand that service standards may differ between London and Dubai/UAE, but the cleanliness, maintenance, service, and attention to detail did not consistently reflect what I would expect from a four-star Accor hotel. At times, the experience felt closer to basic/student accommodation, with the hospitality element missing.

The hotel is large and has great potential, and we did meet some excellent staff. I am sharing this feedback constructively and hope management will take these points seriously and use them to improve the guest experience and better recognise loyal Accor members.

regards 

Nadeem Ahmad

author: John W
title: A positive, comfortable stay in a conveniently located hotel
text: As I had paid extra for early check in , the process was seamy! I still don’t agree with being charged£50 per night holding fee even though the room had been paid for. Reception area is spacious with friendly staff .the room was also spacious with a comfortable bed, which had a convenient plug point by the bed. Both room and bathroom were clean with a/c available. Coffee/tea provided as well as water in the mini fridge. The safe however did not work. There was also an iron and hairdryer and Rituals shower gel, shampoo and body lotion. Ample towels were provided however the bath/shower lacked a bath mat which made it slippery to have a shower. The hotel is convenient to public transport and shops!

author: Roberto B
title: Excellent accommodation
text: Modern hotel located in an excellent position. Comfortable rooms and bathroom and good cleanliness. Very satisfactory welcome with check-in carried out by Maria. Breakfast enjoyed only one day, satisfactory in the quality and quantity of the food, but the room used for it was a bit too chaotic.

author: Aventuraviajero
title: They take deposits and you struggle to get it back
text:
This hotel took a deposit of £50 for each day I stayed, This was on top of charging me for the room on checking in. That was money I needed for my trip. It was in my budget. Why take this deposit? They assured me the deposit would be returned to my account a few days ago. They have not returned it despite my messages asking for it. Now I could end up in a dispute with them. I don't remember other hotels taking a deposit from me.

And, BTW, the room was not very good. It was getting shabby and I do not think they give it maintenance. I do not see this hotel as 4 star but 3 star.

author: Özgür TUNCAY
title: Comfortable Stay with Excellent Transport Links
text:
Comfortable Stay with Excellent Transport Links

We had a very comfortable stay at Novotel London West. One of the biggest advantages of the hotel is its location. Hammersmith Underground Station is just a short walk away, and the Piccadilly Line provides a direct and convenient connection to central London, making it very easy to explore the city.

The Hammersmith area itself is also a great place to stay. There are plenty of pubs, bars, restaurants and cafés nearby, so even after returning from a busy day of sightseeing, there are many places within walking distance to enjoy the evening.

The hotel was comfortable, clean and relaxing, and our room provided a very pleasant place to rest after long days exploring London.

Overall, Novotel London West offers a very good combination of comfort, location and easy access to public transport. Being able to reach central London so easily while staying in the lively Hammersmith area was a real advantage. I would happily stay here again on my next visit to London.

author: rh14n
title: Good location and lovely hotel
text:
Location of this hotel is excellent. Close to Tower of London, Tower Bridge, The Shard and Bishopsgate. Also a 2 minute walk from Tower Hill tube station which is takes you on the district and the circle line. The rooms were lovely and spacious and clean. Stocked with hand wash shampoo, shower gel, fresh towels daily. Also had tea and coffee making facilities in the room, a mini fridge, a hairdryer and an iron.
We opted for breakfast at the Hotel one morning and it was very good with everything you could possibly want for full cooked breakfast and continental options. We also ate at the Natural Kitchen,  the restaurant in the hotel and their staff were lovely and the food was wonderful.
Not in a noisy or extremely street or part of London. 
Very good value for money for location and convenience and great staff.

author: User1882
title: Unhygienic, noisy, unfit stay
text:
Had to leave this hotel early due to unacceptable conditions.

There were mice running around the room overnight, with visible droppings on the carpet. The bathroom plumbing made constant loud churning noises, making it impossible to sleep, and there was no hot water.

Basic facilities were missing — no fridge, no toaster, and reception couldn’t even provide cutlery. I must add however, all the staff I interacted with were lovely and polite and very respectful and helpful. 

I am a type 1 diabetic, so access to food and basic facilities is essential, not optional. I was also staying here before a fight, and the lack of sleep and proper facilities had a direct negative impact on my preparation.

This was far below any acceptable standard. I would strongly advise others to avoid.

author: stevebintley
title: Cheap but dated and tatty
text:
I had a pretty terrible start here, with long queues to check in and being allocated a room on floor minus two. This room had no windows, was lit rather dimly and had zero mobile reception or wifi coverage. Reception offered me an ‘upgraded’ room for an additional thirty pounds a night, and instead I stayed on the top floor with nice views of the waterways below.

It’s fair to say the whole hotel needs a refresh. There was a bit of a stuffy smell in the room, paint needs touching up and wallpaper is peeling in areas, the white fixtures in the bathroom have long turned yellow / stained and features like the air-conditioning control unit were no longer functioning. Saying that though, everywhere was clean and the bed was super comfortable. Electric sockets were next to the bed along with USB ports and a separate fan was available with the hot weather. Iron and board were in the wardrobe along with some biscuits with the drink facilities.

The TV is a bit difficult to see from the bed and the toiletries are in small bottles which are a bit of a pain to use, given they’re not squeezable. However the sleep quality was great, no noise from outside and the room was fairly spacious.

I went for a pizza one evening in the Italian restaurant on the ground floor. Service was pretty slow and expect to have to call waiting staff over whenever you want something, and the pizza was served exceptionally quick after around five minutes. The toppings didn’t taste the freshest, with the ham on the Hawaiian seeming to be the wafer thin processed variety squeezed together, but it was a good size. Bottles of wine were presented in a bucket and stand next to the table which was a good touch. 

There’s some nice seating in the bar area, overlooking the water. Sofas and individual armchairs are comfortable and there’s a really relaxing atmosphere. While there’s no table service, the staff behind the bar are super friendly and happy to engage in actual conversation, but annoying it all closes at 11pm.

Overall it was an okay stay for the price. I can imagine it was fairly grand back in the day but could do with some attention now. Even cleaning the gold chrome around the lobby would help, since it’s covered in year’s worth of finger prints. If the price was right I’d stay again, but I fear it does depend on the room you get allocated.

author: Amy T
title: Exceptional kindness and outstanding customer service
text:
Exceptional kindness and outstanding customer service

Although I was unfortunately unable to stay due to a family medical emergency, I felt compelled to leave a review because of the exceptional kindness and compassion shown by the hotel team.

When I explained that my mother had become seriously ill, Simona Mihalache, the Front Office and Reservations Manager, responded with genuine empathy and immediately cancelled my reservation free of charge as a gesture of goodwill. During an incredibly stressful time, this act of understanding meant so much to me and my family.

It’s easy to review a hotel after a stay, but I believe the true measure of hospitality is how people treat you when unexpected circumstances arise. The professionalism, warmth, and compassion I experienced have left a lasting impression.

Thank you again to Simona and the entire team for your kindness. I sincerely hope to visit in the future under much happier circumstances, and I would not hesitate to recommend this hotel based on the outstanding customer care I received.

author: Sandra M
title: Not enough beds!!
text:
Telephoned before arrival to check if we could have an early check in or if not, could we leave our bags.  Was told an early check would cost extra. Upon arrival to drop off our bags, told our room was not ready anyway. Travelled as family of 5, myself, my daughter & 3 grandchildren.  Told reception we would be late back as we'd booked Harry Potter studios. Arrived back at hotel approx 10pm to find our room had 2 double beds only.  Rang reception & someone came to our room with a travel cot, youngest granddaughter is 7!!. Said this was not acceptable,  only to be told there was nothing they could do as housekeeping had gone home. Asked for another room but was told there would be a discounted charge of £100 which was totally unacceptable as we'd booked & paid for 5 people. Best they could eventually do after nearly an hour was to give us a mattress, quilt etc for the floor. My daughter emailed upon our return home to complain, only to get a response from the hotel that it was our own fault that we didn't notify we needed 5 beds. If the booking is made for 5 people, then surely it's a given you need 5 beds!  Very poor customer service Corus Hotel. 
Location of hotel was good, very close to Hyde Park but based on the treatment we received, will not return.

Could hardly see out the windows (luckily) as they were that dirty. Breakfast was appalling. No plates on our first morning. Bacon like leather, cold tea and coffee , green looking scrambled eggs. The sides hadnt been cleaned properly so when we put our (expensive) photo down that we had got from one of the attractions, it became stuck and tore when trying to get it off. The twin rooms are only suitable if you know youre travelling companion well as the beds are up against each other. We both got bitten a few times. Yes, it was unprecedented heat and the rooms were uncomfortably warm but the fans and keeping curtains closed helped.

author: Keith
title: Good value budget hotel.
text:
This hotel is situated in a very affluent part of London, near to Primrose Hill. There is an underground station about 15 minutes walk away, and it’s a 15 minute ride into town.
Price wise it is a budget hotel, and we paid around £120 a night each for single rooms. Included in the price was the coach journey to and from Glasgow, as well as all you can eat breakfast and evening meal buffets.
The food was of a perfectly reasonable standard bearing in mind the price, and there was a good choice of dishes. Breakfast displayed a comprehensive variety of English and continental breakfasts. Unfortunately the one criticism of breakfast was that all the fried eggs were overcooked until rubbery. Please note that a lot of British consumers like fried eggs more runny than those provided.
The room was spacious, the bed comfortable and the shower excellent.
The weather was remarkably hot, and although there was no air conditioning fans were provided, which, when well positioned, kept the room at a bearable temperature throughout the night.
The staff were pleasant and helpful.
Considering that many Airbnbs in the area advertise rooms with no private bathroom or dining for at least £100 a night, this hotel is definitely good value.

author: Linda B
title: Please ignore the negative reviewers!
text:
Have just returned from a four night stay with Caledonian Travel. This short break was extremely good value and included dinner, bed and breakfast with inclusive coach travel from Glasgow.
Having read the many negative reviews, we were somewhat apprehensive but, on arrival, we were pleasantly surprised by the very pleasant reception and lounge bar area. Our rooms had obviously been recently refurbished (there is currently scaffolding at the front of the hotel which suggests that the whole hotel is currently undergoing an upgrade). We had good sized rooms with a pleasant modern  en-suite shower room with plenty of hot water, very comfortable bed and pillows, a good powerful hair dryer and tea/coffee making facilities. Although the windows in the rooms could not open, a fan was provided which provided adequate air movement and room cooling…..even in the middle of a 33 degree heatwave!
The food, for a budget-priced hotel,  was buffet-style at both breakfast and evening dinner. Breakfast was particularly comprehensive, offering mixed cereal ,fruit,  and a variety of cooked dishes. There was always something to be found at the evening meal with a choice of main course and  potatoes/chips along with nice a soup and fresh salad, hot pudding (which I didn’t try),  fresh fruit, and cheese and biscuits.
This hotel is located in a very residential area of London and is within easy walking of Chalk Road underground station, Primrose Hill, Camden Lock and Market and Camden Town itself,
