author: Matthieu K
title: Excellent!
text: Excellent Welcoming, all the staff were very friendly and ready to render Service, clean room and shower room, varied and fresh breakfast buffet, perfect to start the day. I recommend!

author: Daniel A
title: Unsanitary room
text:
I rarely leave negative reviews, but after my experience at The Washington NYC, I feel obligated to warn future guests.
My son and I had just completed a cross-country drive from San Antonio, Texas. After checking into the hotel around 7:00 PM, we immediately left to visit the One World Observatory and the 9/11 Memorial. As a 100% disabled U.S. Navy veteran and medically retired LAPD police officer, paying tribute at the memorial was one of the main reasons for our trip.
When we returned to our room around 9:30 PM and had a chance to actually look around, we were shocked. The room was filthy. There were boogers and what appeared to be other bodily fluids on the walls and doors, dried food residue on multiple surfaces, what appeared to be feces on the wall next to the toilet, black mold in the shower, stained curtains, and a refrigerator that smelled like a dead animal. It honestly looked like the room hadn't been properly cleaned in a very long time.
I immediately contacted the front desk. After waiting approximately 20–30 minutes, we were moved to another room, and I was assured it had been cleaned.
Unfortunately, the second room was nearly identical. Once again, there were boogers on the walls and doors, food residue on the walls, dirty and stained curtains and bedding, unpleasant odors, and an overall feeling that the room had not been sanitized. By this point it was nearly 11:00 PM. My son was exhausted after our long day and had already fallen asleep. After traveling across the country, moving to a third room late at night was simply not a realistic option, especially after seeing the condition of the first two rooms.
I also contacted Priceline, but our call was disconnected before the issue could be resolved. We checked out early the next morning because we could not wait to leave.
Since then, I have repeatedly tried to speak with the hotel manager—on the night of my stay, the following morning, throughout the day, and again afterward—but no one has returned my calls. At this point, I'm not even convinced there is a manager available to address guest concerns.
I've stayed in countless hotels throughout my military service, law enforcement career, and personal travels, and I can honestly say this was one of the most unsanitary hotel experiences I've ever had. The condition of not just one, but two rooms raises serious concerns about the hotel's cleaning standards.
I have photographs documenting the conditions I encountered.
The location is excellent if you're visiting the World Trade Center and Lower Manhattan, but that does not make up for the deplorable state of the rooms or the complete lack of management response.
I cannot recommend this hotel to anyone until significant improvements are made to its cleanliness and customer service.

author: Shan mattis
title: Spend the extra money for somewhere nicer
text:
I’ve previously stayed here due to location being perfect for access to everything including 9/11 memorial, close to Brooklyn bridge, Wall Street, trains straight to mid-town etc. The first time was manageable (2024) minus a few issues. However staying there this year seemed that they lowered their standards to the floor. 

Not only did we request to change our room four times…before we had even been there an hour due to stains in the sheets, holes in the bed, tears in the sheets, missing fridges, filthy bathrooms or smells but the the comfort of the room is terrible. For the amount of money you spend to stay here you might as well of slept on the bench across the road. 

The staff were as helpful as they possibly could have been but you can tell they all just don’t care. 

Out of six lifts present in the hotel. Two worked. 

One in the main entrance and one other to get you from the lobby to the rest of the 50 odd floors. You will be waiting a significant amount of time just to get in or out of the hotel. 

It has a gym which can be accessed, pretty standard. They do not have a breakfast/eating facilities on site. Eating out is necessary but this is expected with this type of trip. 

Overall, the first time I would have given it 5/10 just for the fact it was my first time in NYC. But I most certainly will NEVER be staying here again. -1000/10

author: Angela L
title: No luxury here. Just handy and pretty rough and worn out.
text:
A bit dated and in need of better lighting and a very good deep clean. Bathroom was dimly lit. Hairdryer was all noise and no action. No iron. No coffee making or even a kettle. ( After long flight this would have been nice)
Dated furniture in the guest lounge, all seen better days. Lighting terrible. Less than interactive staff. Door man was the friendliest. On pulling up, it looked closed. Carpets and lift all need revamp. If you want luxury, move on, you won't find it here. Lifts are slow DnD often out of service. Housekeepers were lovely and made up our room. We had plenty of towels, but given time, they don't have chance to deep clean bathrooms and floor was slippery when wet!!! Yuk.
Very close to the 9/11 memorial and for food Flavor Deli is open 24/7. Great food, fab staff, good prices. No services at this hotel. Also close to O Haras Irish bar for good and a drink. Well placed, but past it's best.

author: Giarca
title: Shut them down.
text: Absolutely the worst Hotel I’ve ever had the displeasure of staying at. The staff is about as friendly as a pile of rhinoceros feces, and they are as honest as the Trump administration. After barely honoring my reservation, they stuck me in the worst room hotel that had no air-conditioning. I tried for over 24 hours to resolve the situation until they finally moved me into another room. The servers been admitted, but the air-conditioning didn’t work and that the thermostat was broken in the day were not able to get a part to repair it. I tried to have that first night refunded to me and they refused. I’m in the process now of suing them.

author: Jonathan B
title: Don’t understand the hate!  This place is fantastic value for money
text: I don’t understand all the hate and complaints in the reviews.  I had a great stay here in April.  Large room with a king sized bed, great views and clean bathroom and closet.  Friendly and accommodating staff, efficient room cleaning, and super location.  It’s a tad inefficient getting to the rooms with two elevators but frankly I’ve stayed in Ritz Carlton hotels with the same thing.  This is an excellent value for money.  You will be hard pressed to find a hotel room in New York as nice as this at this price point.

author: Jake S
title: The best view of the trevi fountain
text: Perfect location and incredible views

author: AKA
title: Right at the Trevi
text: Trevi fountain right outside the front door. Staff was pleasant, room was clean. Lots of activity in the area, a little difficult for automobile pickups and drop offs but not impossible.

author: Extraordinary732574
title: Avoid
text: The hotel is in a great location opposite the Trevi fountain but that is all it has going for it. The hotel is dark and dingy and smells of mould. Furniture is old and broken, paint is peeling from the walls. The bathroom was damp and in desperate need of an upgrade with mouldy sealant when present. Room was cleaned daily with a fresh threadbare towels left to use. Breakfast staff were lovely but the man at reception was rude and aggressive. Tourist tax had to be paid in cash only! Be aware that due to the location the hotel is very noisy throughout the day and night.

author: LoveTravel746809
title: Best spot with the worst service.
text: This is the best spot in Rome with the worst service possible. They behaved like they were  tired of tourists. We pay $25 per person to visit the rooftop and had the worst experience ever.  They included 1 drink and a snack with the price, however they didn't have most of the drinks in the menu. No whiskey, no rum, no tequila, no coke and the peanuts were soggy. Basically you are almost obligated to have a spritz and a bag of potato ships. The lady was not happy with us and we were the only group  in the room (4). The view is beautiful, but we were not allowed to take pictures or basically to move in the room. The room was hot and the a/c is too small to cool the space. Visit is not recommended at all.

author: Tanya Ball
title: Just returned from a lovely 3 night stay at this lovely, quirky, welcoming hotel
text:
We have just returned from a 3 nights stay at this lovely, quirky, welcoming hotel.
Yes, this is an old building but it adds to the charm of this hotel. 
We were a family of 4 staying in 3 rooms 103 & 104. Both had comfortable beds and were very clean.
All the staff on reception were very welcoming and friendly and happy to help with any questions or queries.
Every morning we injoyed our continental breakfast overlooking the trevi fountain, the ladies who looked after our every need were very accommadating and very friendly. 
This hotel is a situated in a perfect location to enjoy all the best sites of Rome! 
You can step outside and join the buzzing atmosphere of the city on your doorstep then retreat back into a quaint hotel and relax in a cool airy relaxing room.
Would we recommend? Yes!
Would we return? Absolutely!

author: Holly W.
title: Excellent Boutique Hotel
text: Hotel Santa Maria is the CUTEST boutique hotel nestled within the alley way of Trastevere. We thoroughly enjoyed our stay. The staff was so accommodating and friendly and Kevin (the bartender) was seriously the best! The breakfast and aperitifs were great! He gave us phenomenal service and we had so much fun! 10/10 would stay there again and highly recommend!

author: Jim B
title: Wonderful Place!!
text:
I just spent five nights at this beautiful little oasis in the heart Trastevere. I could not have been happier or more comfortable. A stunning, quiet, haven from the August heat with cool aspect and orange trees - it was an absolute pleasure!!
It would be unfair to single out staff members by name because everyone from the reception staff to those who served the complimentary breakfast (and the delicious cocktails), to those who kept the rooms and grounds clean and fresh were super friendly, helpful, kind and considerate. I send them all my heartfelt thanks and best wishes - and I really hope to be able to stay here again in the future.

author: Rachel J
title: Amazing
text: Excellent location, unbeatable service, absolute delight to stay here.

author: Elena García
title: A charming and peaceful stay in Trastevere
text:
My boyfriend and I stayed at Hotel Santa Maria, and we had a wonderful experience. The hotel is beautiful, peaceful, and full of character, with a lovely courtyard that makes it feel like a hidden oasis in the heart of Trastevere.

The room was clean, comfortable, and quiet, and the staff were exceptionally friendly and helpful throughout our stay. The location is perfect for exploring Rome, with many restaurants, cafés, and attractions within walking distance.

As a traveler, I truly appreciated the warm atmosphere and the excellent hospitality. We felt very welcome and enjoyed every moment of our stay. I would highly recommend Hotel Santa Maria to couples looking for a relaxing and memorable stay in Rome, and we would definitely return.

author: notsofussy186605
title: A calm little oasis in Trastevere
text:
Hotel Santa Maria was wonderful. It's set in a little oasis in the middle of Trastevere. It's not the easiest to reach by car, but the taxi dropped us in front without any trouble.
The staff were really friendly, the buffet breakfast was wonderful, and the evening cocktails/apeo were welcome after a lonf day sightseeing  — I'll miss my basil smash. The rooms very clean, and the whole place feels calm. It's not modern — but that's exactly the charm. A really special stay.

author: Deb P
title: Very nice hotel in a great location!
text: Kadesha and T'sai were excellent!  They were very helpful in accommodating our request for a higher room to avoid noise.  They were so professional and kind.  I wish all hotel staff were as dedicated to customer satisfaction.  The rooms were very clean, and the beds were incredibly comfortable.  The high end hair dryer and steamer were a nice touch. (The doorless shower was a little awkward, but we proactively put towels down to catch the splashing.) The windows are not soundproof, so you may want to bring a noise machine.  But there wasn't too much noise from Port Authority.  (the location is excellent if you are going to Broadway!) The $25 daily food credit was very nice, and the "to go" sandwiches were delicious!  The gym is spacious, and the equipment is in great condition.  And I didn't have a problem with the elevators, even though we were on the 31st floor.  The fee is reasonable, and I would come back here again.  Thank you!

author: Journey04798699082
title: Worst experience of our life
text: This trip has been hell. There is a protest going on outside the hotel 24/7 and we were never warned, even though it was going on when we booked. We cannot sleep a wink. They have drums and are screaming. They have saucepans and are blowing whistles. I cannot believe we paid so much for this. They refused to put us at the back of the hotel when we asked.

author: richvinrootjr
title: Great Bonvoy stay in NYC. Very good location. Very nice staff. Great little bar. Very convenient and well priced for NYC
text: Excellent locale and Value in Times Square

author: Sandrine M
title: Wonderful 3 night stay at the Delta Hotel
text: Spent three nights with my daughter at the Delta hotel. The price to quality ratio is excellent. The hotel is located by the neighborhood of Hell’s Kitchen on one side which offers many moderately priced ethnic restaurants. On the other side, just a short walk away from Times Square and broadway shows. Our room on the 26th floor was well equipped and quiet. The desk is large enough to do some work. I would definitely consider staying again at the Delta hotel.

author: 45ier
title: Would Stay Again
text: This was my first time staying at a Delta hotel and i will definitely be back. Location location location, is everything while in Manhattan and this property was in the center of it all. Nicole and team were great even allowed an early check-in. The bathroom situation as a little strange with no shower door, but it worked. I visit NYC a lot and this was probably one of the larger of the rooms that i have been in. Overall, when looking for a place to stay within the Marriott family, I always hope this property is available.

author: Glyn M
title: Beautiful hotel, wonderful staff
text: I travel the world and stay in some of the finest hotels around; and after my recent stay at the Aman NYC, I’m blown away! The hospitality was second to none. The food was a delight and daily highlight! Beautiful suit and fantastically located on 5th Ave next to Central Park. I can’t recommend the Aman enough!

author: Quest48474255356
title: total joke and laughingstock
text:
It was a total waste of money. This place is a total joke and laughingstock, but with extraordinary pricing. As we look at the reviews here, the local management doesn't give a sh*t about guest opinions... Maybe international management will take a look someday. A hotel isn't about walls, expensive furniture, or artificial scent, but "luxury is in the detail"; it's about the people, the workers. And the workers here are terrible (very young, except crazy safety team)! We arrived at night on the weekend, and an angry security guard started an interrogation.... It was NIGHT! We told him about our reservation, but he tried to send us to the residential part of this building (we do not why). Maitre d' was useless, an 18-year-old-like non-binary person, just was smiling.
At the front desk, we had a problem with our reservation (correct - they had!). A nice-looking lady couldn't find something in their system and asked us to wait. It was night, again. After our flight! Then her manager—the guy with a tired face, black hair (Southern European I think)—started eyerolling... We felt like he is doing a favor to us after paying thousands dollar for night... his attitude was disgusting
Again, it was nighttime; we had just arrived after a flight. So, we waited for a while... But the vibe was crazy... "Sorry for visiting this "luxury" hotel at an inconvenient time for you!" We literally apologized to the workers... But we will never stay in this place again! 
Consider Baccarat, Mandarin, Faena, Rosewood, Astoria (the best so far), Four Seasons... all cheaper, but the employees are professional (and turned out older, so more professional)!
This place is a total joke and has nothing in common with other amans in Europe (Montenegro) or Asia (Japan). 
By the way, it's so noisy to stay here, there are limited food options, and every entrance to the hotel feels like an airport security check... Stay away and save money for better!

author: BayswaterMum
title: Beautiful communal Spaces but clueless staff
text:
This is the most expensive hotel in New York and as such one would expect the service to be amazing sadly although the staff are all very friendly and pleasant they clearly have not received adequate training. Just to reiterate this is not a staff problem per say it’s a management problem.

We arrived on Monday evening and emailed the hotel three times two days ahead of our arrival prior to our departure to arrange an airport transfer from JFK to the hotel which we were more than willing to pay for but they were unable to organise this … this is a basic service that you would expect any 5 star hotel to be able to do.

Due to the non linear layout of the hotel it’s absolutely essential to ask for a tour of the communal facilities on arrival since you can’t rely on there being someone around to assist if you get lost … the lady at reception had apparently never been to the pool what didn’t help is that there are no signs for the pool. 

On arrival on Monday I booked a table for 6 for dinner outside for the Italian restaurant on Wednesday evening. I reconfirmed this on Tuesday and was told absolutely no problem it was all confirmed. 

Wednesday evening arrived and we were shown to a table for 6 inside and told that no one had conveyed our specific request for a table outside and unfortunately it wasn’t possible to now accommodate this request because outside was now full. This was very disappointing because we specifically wanted to eat outside if this wasn’t possible we should have been told on Monday or even Tuesday morning when we.would have gone to either the Colony Club or Soho House instead we were misled causing us disappointment & embarrassment when you paying circa $1000us for a simple dinner not what you would expect. At the end of the meal the staff apologised for the mistake and said we would not be charged for the meal. I am writing this review on Friday morning on the train to Boston after checking out and have gone through the bill on the train and have  noted that we were charged for the meal.

Here’s the thing I was disappointed and slightly annoyed about the mess up with the table booking, but at no point did I ask or indeed expect any financial compensation . Instead I just added it to my impression of the hotel beautiful communal spaces but useless but friendly staff. When the staff actively came and told us on the terrace where we had retired to after dinner that the bill for dinner was on the hotel we were surprised and indeed asked several times are you sure but obviously were grateful and indeed it did achieve the effect of cancelling out any negativity we had about our overall experience of the hotel despite not changing our views as to the hotel being work in progress as far as staff training goes. In fact I was debating about giving the hotel a 5/4 rating. However now that I have seen the bill my husband has insisted that I give a 2 rating on principle because you simply can’t offer financial compensation for poor service and then not actually follow through with it … it’s basically fraud.

Honesty and truth are fundamental principles of all human transactions it would have been better for the hôtel restaurant staff to have offered no compensation especially when I did not  ask for it rather than offer fake compensation.

Moving on from my personal experiences her are my general observations about the hotel compared to other hotels I have stayed at.

1. The communal spaces are beautiful and indeed the outside spaces were much appreciated whilst staying in New York during August.

2. The actual food was very good.

3. The. Lap pool though difficult to locate was actually great.

4. The actual navigation of the hotel wasn’t easy but this is the problem when you are retrofitting an existing building so I am mot criticising merely making an observation.

5. The rooms themselves whilst visually attractive are basically one. Room with the. Bathroom just behind a screen so no chance of using the bathroom  discretely… you can even here the tap running and the screens are translucent so cause light pollution at night.

I am torn about whether I would revisit on my next trip especially at this price .

author: Milian Ritcher
title: True AMAN
text:
Our stay at Aman New York was truly unforgettable. From the moment we arrived, we were welcomed with warm and professional service that made us feel incredibly special. The hotel is absolutely beautiful, with a luxurious and peaceful atmosphere that feels like a true escape in the heart of New York City.

The rooms were stunning, comfortable, and thoughtfully designed, with every detail carefully considered. The staff was attentive, kind, and always willing to help, making sure everything was perfect throughout our stay.

What impressed us the most was the combination of luxury, privacy, and exceptional service. Even though you are in the middle of Manhattan, the hotel feels calm and relaxing. Every part of our experience was special, and we truly enjoyed our time there.

Thank you to the entire team at Aman New York for making our stay so memorable. We look forward to coming back again.

author: Mike
title: Amazing hotel, highly recommended
text: Amazing hotel with great service and fantastic food! Highly recommended! It doesn’t have a lot of rooms, so you should book in advance, built it worths to go there

author: Meander05031522788
title: A Confirmed Booking Meant Nothing
text: One month after my confirmed reservation, the property cancelled my booking, citing a “system error”. Meanwhile, the room was being offered again at a much higher price. This was extremely disappointing and demonstrated a lack of reliability. I definitely do not recommend this place.

author: Oren P
title: Scam Alert: Do not book here. They will force you to pay for their broken rooms.
text:
Save your money and book somewhere else. This hostel uses predatory bait-and-switch tactics to squeeze extra cash out of exhausted travelers.
When I checked in, the AC and fan in my room were completely dead. The room was a sauna. I went to the desk, but instead of apologizing or moving me, the staff strung me along for two hours making up ridiculous excuses—like claiming a broken AC "takes 30 minutes to get going."
When they finally admitted the room was uninhabitable, they refused to move me to a working room unless I paid them an additional $30 "upgrade fee." It was past midnight, I was dead tired, and they essentially held a safe, cool room hostage until I handed over more money. I was forced to pay it just to get some sleep.
The kicker? The AC in the "upgraded" room was broken, too. I spent the entire night sweating in a sweltering room after being scammed into paying a premium for air conditioning they didn't even provide.
Management clearly does not care about guest comfort or fulfilling basic reservations; they only care about extracting hidden fees when you are too tired to fight back. Avoid this place at all costs unless you want to pay extra for the privilege of sleeping in an oven.

author: Julius J
title: Great location and clean facilities, but beds might fall short of expectations
text:
Location is excellent, and the facilities are clean and well-maintained. There’s a kitchen area and a lounge space where you can work, which is a nice bonus. The staff were friendly and helpful—for example, they adjusted the air conditioning in the evening upon request.

The only downside is that the beds didn’t match what you could expect from the website and their advertising material. I was anticipating capsule-style beds that can be fully enclosed and dark, but in my room they were regular bunk beds with a small curtain covering only about one-third of the bed length. As other reviewers have mentioned, there's only a thin sheet + a polyester blanket.

author: Linda Schuyler Ford
title: Cozy bed, Bright Lights
text:
The location is great, with easy walking to theaters, Times Square and Central Park. I was in a quad room which was very clean, as was our bathroom.

5he one 5hing that brought down my rating is, the bright ceiling lights are on motion sensors.  Not only did the lights come on when a guest arrived late, or when someone got up to use the restroom-they came on every single time I moved in my lower bunk! Several times a night. A curtain covers half of each bunk' giving some privacy but not prote lion from bright lights. Sleep masks are available but I thought they were more a gimmick. Even using one the second night only helped a bit. I still woke each time the lights came on. Surely there is a reasonable fix for this.

Location, price (still not cheap) and cleanliness would bring me back again. I just will not expect a good night's sleep.

author: LuckyLuke040
title: Very convenient
text:
Handy if you have very little time in New York, I was there for an afternoon and evening and still wanted to take a shower somewhere and leave my luggage before I went into town.
You have a bed with light and sockets, and a locker. With a curtain it is separated from the hallway. The shower and toilet are in the hallway and in my case shared with another 'pod'.
The clean, quiet, fine shower, affordable and 5 minute walk to Central Park and 10 minute to Times Square.

author: AddieCMomOfThree
title: A solid choice - a very good value for a new, clean and comfortable room in a convenient location
text: Stayed in a city view, two queens room for two nights. New, clean, and a pretty decent size, for a NYC hotel room. The beds were comfortable, and the A/C ran quietly (NOT the kind which continuously cycles on and off). We stayed on the 13th floor, and the street noise wasn't too bad. We could have used more hooks in the bathroom though (I think there was only one), so there weren't enough places to hang all our towels in the bathroom. Took off one star off because the room was not ready by the 4:00pm check-in time, and the elevators were a bit slow (one of the three elevators was out of service). Front desk was friendly, but they could have been more helpful in explaining how the elevators worked and mentioning that there was coffee available in the mornings and a water machine in the food area. A good value and in a convenient location, near major subway lines and a 10-minute walk from Moynihan Train Hall.

author: sonia b
title: Hotel right in the city center
text: Nice hotel, the view from the room is magnificent, very clean. Pleasant staff. Very disappointing breakfast. We had to buy food for the morning. Little choice. Needs more effort! No parking.

author: Chrystel2014
title: Very good location and good bedding
text: Great location to visit New York. Quiet street in the center of New York. Located in the flower district. Metro line 1 around the corner 3 minutes walk. The bedding is good. Shower room correct, a little small. On the other hand no storage in the bedroom or in the shower room. It was quite embarrassing to have to open the suitcases every day, especially when you stay 1 week. But otherwise we really enjoyed the situation and the bedding.

author: brett M
title: Couple of Kiwis in NYC
text:
Whole stay was excellent 
Shout out to the amazing Tara!  at the hotel bar 
arriving back after a long day sightseeing was nice to see a friendly face and have a chat and of course help with fantastic drinks choices 
She knows her stuff!

author: Shaun S
title: The flower district is a great option
text:
Out of the Marriott tiers, Aloft is a more basic option; however, the Chelsea location is pretty decent. 

Pros include location and nice folks at the front desk. 

Negatives include the cost and the low quality furnishings. 

Still, not bad.

author: Michelle C
title: They lie. Avoid
text: This was horrible. There is no air conditioning, we had a heat wave. They didn't care and would not refund or compensate. They also waited until I checked in to disclose. The entire stay was bad. Broken shower, dirty room. The staff are horrible. AVOID.

author: René B
title: Book a better neighbourhood.
text:
The hotel is located at the start of Pigalle, the Red Light district.   What attracted me initially was the decor, each room decorated in the style of a famous artist.   We stayed in room 304, the Augustine Renoir room.   Small, ideal for one or two nights, no more.   Air Con was out of action for the previous 2 months which in August heat was terrible.   Lots of homeless and immigrants hanging out at the little fountain outside a noisy at night.  Not recommended for solo travellers as seen someone robbed as drunk by a guy going over offering to help him.   Paris in general is expensive.  Lots of good places have queues outside at all times of the day.   Moulin Rouge 5 minutes walk away.

Best little cocktail bar nearby is an unassuming place called ‘Dirty Dick’, not a gay bar! But with the cheap cocktails starting at €17 a pop, we had 2 each and left.  Bring a good pair of walking shoes, the subway system can be tricky to navigate and unless you know the zone your travelling, your better off getting a day pass.

Flat rate to the airport is meant to be €56.  Hotel advertises it at €63, driver charged us €72.

Took 30 minutes and not up to 3 hours as advertised on some reviews.   Safe too than the RER B train at €14 per person one way and we saw someone robbed on the train out from the airport.
